name: Malene Søiland
summary: Malene Søiland studies nursing leadership, focusing on how registered nurses without formal leadership roles take on leadership in everyday work. Using qualitative methods, including individual interviews, a hermeneutical approach and thematic analysis, her research examines home healthcare settings in Norwegian municipalities. The work looks at how nurses share responsibility, keep track of care tasks and organise their work under time limits.

name: Margareth Kristoffersen
summary: Margareth Kristoffersen conducts qualitative research on nursing and health professional practice in Norway, covering nurse leadership in home healthcare, the retention of school nurses, and competence development among health professionals with master's degrees. Her work relies on individual and group interviews analysed with hermeneutic, phenomenological hermeneutic, thematic and discourse analysis approaches. The findings relate to nursing workforce retention, everyday leadership in community care and health science education.

name: Maria Handeland
summary: Maria Handeland researches clinical nursing education, with a focus on how digital educational resources can support nurse educators who oversee students during placements. Her work uses interpretive descriptive qualitative methods, including focus group interviews and thematic analysis, to examine educators' experiences. The application setting is first-year student nurse placements in nursing homes.

name: Marta Høyland Lavik
summary: Marta Høyland Lavik studies how parents experience grief after an infant dies, with a focus on neonatal intensive care in Norway. Her work uses focus group interviews with bereaved parents and reflexive thematic analysis to examine how keepsakes such as clothing, blankets, prints and scrapbooks support remembrance, ritual and continuing bonds, while also provoking mixed and painful emotions. The findings relate to bereavement care practices offered by healthcare professionals.

name: Miguel German Borda Borda
summary: Miguel German Borda Borda studies the links between ageing, muscle health, brain structure and dementia, with a focus on Alzheimer's disease, Lewy body dementia and Parkinson's disease. His work combines MRI-based muscle and brain measurements, EEG spectral analysis, serum metabolite networks and longitudinal and population-based cohorts (such as UK Biobank, SABE Colombia and Norwegian dementia cohorts), analysed with regression, mixed-effects and mediation models. Application areas include early detection and prognosis of cognitive decline, sarcopenia and malnutrition diagnosis, frailty, quality of life and oral and mental health in older adults.

name: Monica Hetlesæther Fosmark
summary: Monica Hetlesæther Fosmark studies perioperative nursing, with a focus on how operating room nurses position patients for robotic-assisted surgery. Her work uses a descriptive qualitative design, drawing on individual interviews with nurses at a university hospital and analysing them through qualitative content analysis. The research addresses patient safety, prevention of positioning injuries, nurse responsibility and teamwork in the operating room.

name: Sebastian Rehnman
summary: Sebastian Rehnman works in philosophy, with publications on how philosophical inquiry can address questions in psychotherapy research and on practicing philosophy through poetry. His work argues that conceptual and philosophical analysis, rather than quantitative or qualitative empirical methods, is needed to clarify the character traits of effective psychotherapists and the behavioral criteria for caring. He also explores poetry as a way of pursuing wisdom about questions of human existence.

name: Signe Østrem
summary: Signe Østrem studies self-care among people with heart failure, with a focus on how nurse-assisted remote patient monitoring shapes their symptom awareness, routines and confidence at home. Her work uses longitudinal qualitative methods, with repeated semi-structured interviews analysed by content analysis, and is linked to a randomised trial of a hospital-to-home eHealth intervention. The findings relate to digital support for transitional care between hospital and home.

name: Silje Espejord
summary: Silje Espejord studies how health professionals work together in antenatal and perinatal care, with a focus on pregnant women in vulnerable situations. The publication shown uses an online questionnaire of Norwegian community midwives, analysed statistically, to map who they collaborate with, how they communicate and which tools they use. The work relates to midwifery practice, integrated care and interprofessional training in primary and maternity health services.

name: Siv Tove Aunan
summary: Siv Tove Aunan studies how women with breast cancer prepare to return to work while still in treatment, using individual interviews and qualitative content analysis. Her work looks at survivors' sense of hope and personal value, and at how workplace contact, continuity of care, and information from healthcare providers shape their experience. The findings are aimed at helping healthcare professionals give individualized guidance on sick leave, legal rights, and support services.

name: Synnøve Mari Eidsvik Folkvord
summary: Synnøve Mari Eidsvik Folkvord studies midwifery education, focusing on simulation-based learning, student-led simulation and the supervision of students in clinical placement. Her work uses qualitative methods such as focus groups, written reflections and narratives analysed thematically, along with a systematic qualitative review. The studies address facilitator training, supervisor courses, student self-efficacy and patient safety in maternity care across European settings.

name: Torhild Borlaug
summary: Torhild Borlaug studies midwifery practice and midwifery education using qualitative methods such as interviews, focus groups and thematic analysis. Her work includes a cross-national interview study with hospital midwives in the Nordic and Baltic regions on how they understand and promote normal, physiological birth. She also examines student-led simulation training in a master's midwifery programme, looking at how a facilitator course shapes students' learning and reflection.

name: Turid Anita Jaastad
summary: Turid Anita Jaastad studies how nursing students develop into professional caring nurses, working within caring science and nurse education. Her work combines a qualitative systematic review with thematic synthesis and qualitative analysis of written student reflections from Norwegian undergraduate programmes. Application areas include reflection groups, role-play simulation and curriculum support for students' professional and personal formation.

name: Aksel Paulsen
summary: Aksel Paulsen studies orthopaedic care and patient-reported outcomes, including ankle fractures, hip and knee arthroplasty, hip fractures and fracture prevention services. The work uses validation studies, systematic reviews, qualitative interviews, cohort analyses, secondary analyses of randomized trials and a trial protocol to assess outcome measures and clinical pathways. It also covers primary care interventions for chronic pain, evaluating feasibility and changes in health literacy.

name: Ane Kristine Bendixen
summary: Ane Kristine Bendixen studies how legal frameworks and human rights apply to municipal health and care services for people with severe mental illness and substance use disorders in Norway. Her work uses qualitative interviews with municipal service providers and county governors' office staff, analysed through systematic text condensation. It identifies practical difficulties with the regulations, including gaps in legal basis, complexity, and reliance on effort beyond minimum legal requirements.

name: Anne Marie Lunde Husebø
summary: Anne Marie Lunde Husebø studies nurse-assisted eHealth and remote patient monitoring for self-management support after hospital discharge, mainly for patients with heart failure and colorectal cancer. Her work combines qualitative, mixed-methods and review approaches with trial protocols and feasibility evaluations, and also covers research recruitment in chronic illness. She has further examined nurses' attitudes to infection control and antibiotic stewardship, and digital educational resources and co-creation for nursing mentorship in nursing homes.

name: Anne Marte Løvik
summary: Anne Marte Løvik studies nursing leadership and workforce retention in Norwegian municipal nursing homes. Her work examines the strategies first-line nursing leaders use to keep nurses in their posts, such as building professional and collegial communities, allowing flexibility in daily work and acting as role models. She analyses these empirical examples through transformational leadership theory, in settings marked by low staffing and patients with complex care needs.

name: Anne Schanche Selbekk
summary: Anne Schanche Selbekk studies recovery, peer support and the experiences of people affected by substance use and mental health problems, including family members and adolescents with parents who have substance use problems. Her work combines qualitative methods (interviews, ethnography, meta-ethnography, discourse analysis) with quasi-experimental and survey-based analyses. Application areas include peer-led courses and Recovery Colleges in community services, gender-sensitive treatment and support, intimate partner violence treatment, and marginalized people in public drug and alcohol scenes in Norway and Denmark.

name: Bente Dahl
summary: Bente Dahl studies maternal, perinatal and early childhood health, with a focus on midwifery care and the lived experiences of parents and healthcare providers. Her work relies mainly on qualitative evidence synthesis, including meta-ethnography and a mapping review of phenomenological studies, alongside interview-based research with women in rural Norway. Topics include fetal death, alcohol use in pregnancy, access to birthing facilities in remote areas, and infant mental health.

name: Bente Hamre Larsen
summary: Bente Hamre Larsen studies how health needs of older adults living at home are assessed, with a focus on training healthcare professionals such as nurses, physiotherapists and occupational therapists to carry out interprofessional, holistic assessments. Her work uses qualitative methods including thematic analysis of simulation debriefings, a scoping review of training approaches, and a pre-post study protocol combining quantitative frailty measures with interviews. The application setting is municipal health and care services in Norway, aimed at supporting healthy aging and independent living at home.

name: Bjørg Karlsen
summary: Bjørg Karlsen's research centres on nurse-assisted eHealth and remote patient monitoring for people with chronic illness, especially heart failure and colorectal cancer after hospital discharge. Her work includes randomised and feasibility trial protocols, mixed methods analyses of nurse work and intervention use, and systematic, integrative and scoping reviews, including a taxonomy of research recruitment in chronic illness studies. She also writes theoretical discussion papers on the concepts of disease and diagnosis in nursing.

name: Britt Marit Haga
summary: Britt Marit Haga conducts qualitative caring science research on health, suffering and meaning in life, with a focus on how men in Norway experience loss and major life transitions. Her studies use in-depth interviews and reflexive thematic analysis, drawing on Eriksson's caritative caring theory and Erikson's theory, and she has also used focus groups with a phenomenological-hermeneutical approach. She has examined how health professionals reflect on existential concerns among people with obesity in lifestyle change programmes.

name: Christophe Eward Kattouw
summary: Christophe Eward Kattouw studies how home-based care and community services for older adults can be reshaped to match what senior citizens and other stakeholders prefer. The publications use qualitative interviews with content analysis and service design workshops with thematic analysis, involving older people, carers, health professionals, municipal managers and transport providers in Norway. Application areas include timely home care, continuity of services, age-friendly mobility and housing, and design principles and prototypes for municipal service planning.

name: Edvin Bru
summary: Edvin Bru studies how classroom relationships, teacher support, social-emotional competencies and growth mindset relate to academic engagement, well-being, achievement and school or university dropout among adolescents and first-year students in Norway. The work relies mainly on longitudinal and cross-sectional survey data analysed with structural equation, latent change score and cross-lagged panel models, alongside qualitative focus-group studies of school-based social-emotional learning programmes. A smaller strand covers health research, including an eHealth trial protocol, studies of cancer-related fatigue and treatment burden, and lifestyle change at a healthy life centre.

name: Eirik Haarr
summary: Eirik Haarr studies how opioids are prescribed and used in Norway, drawing on national registers, hospital procurement data and tender agreements. His work compares oxycodone and morphine use across hospitals and primary care, and uses linked register cohorts with survival analysis to examine substance use disorders among people on long-term opioid treatment and the socioeconomic and clinical factors linked to them. His publications also include commentary on artificial intelligence and on smoking legislation.

name: Elisabeth Lind Melbye
summary: Elisabeth Lind Melbye studies oral health and quality of life in older adults and dental implant patients, and the use of digital tools in nursing home care. Her work uses surveys, factor analysis, regression models, questionnaire validation and a cluster randomised trial in Norwegian settings. Application areas include peri-implant disease outcomes, oral care for nursing home residents, caregiver acceptance of mobile health apps, and information sharing between health and kitchen personnel.

name: Flora Balieva
summary: Flora Balieva studies the psychological, social and economic burden of skin disease, with a focus on psychodermatology. Her work uses large multicentre cross-sectional questionnaire studies across Europe, Norwegian national patient register follow-up, surveys with cost estimation, and qualitative interviews. Topics include stigmatization, perceived stress, itch, body dysmorphic concerns and psychiatric comorbidity in conditions such as alopecia areata, psoriasis, hidradenitis suppurativa and prurigo, as well as service provision and classification in psychodermatology.

name: Gudrun Songøygard Battin
summary: Gudrun Songøygard Battin studies interprofessional teamwork in biopsychosocial rehabilitation for chronic pain. Using ethnographic fieldwork, including participant observation and interviews with professionals and patients, she examines how team members negotiate time and workspace and how patients experience encounters with teams in relation to pain stigma. The work applies thematic analysis to a hospital pain rehabilitation ward setting.

name: Heidi Dombestein
summary: Heidi Dombestein studies resilience in healthcare and how adaptive capacity supports high-quality, safe care, mainly in Norwegian homecare, nursing homes and hospitals. Her work uses qualitative designs such as multiple case studies, focus groups, interviews, workshop observation and stakeholder analysis, alongside systematic, scoping and narrative reviews. Topics include risk perception among homecare leaders and professionals, management and champions, patient and family involvement, learning tools for putting resilience into practice, and patient and caregiver experiences in stroke and dementia care.

name: Hildegunn Sagvaag
summary: Hildegunn Sagvaag studies recovery, peer support and services for people with substance use and mental health problems, including supported housing, legal frameworks and coercion in municipal care. Her work uses qualitative interviews, narrative and action research approaches, scoping and systematic reviews, and quasi-experimental and multilevel statistical analyses. She also examines alcohol use in workplaces, covering sickness absence and drinking culture, as well as the translation of a peer-led recovery course into a Norwegian setting.

name: Inge Joa
summary: Inge Joa studies psychosis and schizophrenia spectrum disorders, with a focus on early intervention, clinical insight, cognition, childhood trauma and help-seeking. Much of the work draws on the BeSt InTro antipsychotic trial, using regression, mixed-effects and growth curve models to compare amisulpride, aripiprazole and olanzapine and to relate treatment to symptoms, cytokines, cellular adhesion molecules and blood gene expression. She also conducts implementation research, using trials, cohort studies, fidelity measures and qualitative interviews, on evidence-based psychosis treatments, family psychoeducation and a national mental health registry in Norway.

name: Ingrid Elisabeth Mathisen Haaland
summary: Ingrid Elisabeth Mathisen Haaland studies how public health nurses at child health clinics in Norway follow up children and families when there are concerns about a child's care, including possible neglect or maltreatment. The work uses an exploratory qualitative design with focus groups and latent content analysis, drawing on health promotion and child- and family-centered care perspectives. It examines the dilemmas, routines and approaches shaping nursing practice and proposes a model of follow-up to guide future research.

name: Ingrid Ølfarnes Røysland
summary: Ingrid Ølfarnes Røysland conducts qualitative health research on how people experience illness and life disruption, using meta-ethnography, phenomenological hermeneutic interviews and secondary analysis guided by transition theory. Her work examines physical activity and uncertainty in people with unexplained chest pain and microvascular angina, and the effects of parental alienation in childhood on adult self-esteem and well-being. The studies aim to inform person-centred care by nurses and other health and social care professionals.

name: Jorunn Nærland Skjærpe
summary: Jorunn Nærland Skjærpe studies how to support health and care for people with serious mental illness in Norwegian community and municipal services. Her work combines qualitative methods such as interviews, café dialogues, workshops and co-creation with a feasibility study protocol that adds questionnaires, covering care coordination, determinants of health and a digital peer support app called DigiPer. The work involves service users, peer support workers and health professionals.

name: Kristin Hjorthaug
summary: Kristin Hjorthaug studies nursing education and professional development, with a focus on digital storytelling as a way to support reflection in clinical practice. Her work uses exploratory qualitative methods, including focus group interviews analysed through content analysis, to examine how practicing nurses in hospital and nursing home settings respond to digital stories made by nursing students. The research relates to continuing education for nurses and ways of embedding reflective learning activities in everyday clinical units.

name: Kristin Hjorthaug Urstad
summary: Kristin Hjorthaug Urstad's publications cover health literacy and patient self-management, eHealth support after hospital discharge, and simulation-based nursing and midwifery education. Her work includes randomized trials, quasi-experimental, cross-sectional and qualitative studies, scoping and integrative reviews, and a meta-synthesis. Settings include kidney transplantation, colorectal cancer, heart failure, primary care, parents of toddlers, adolescent health messaging, and nursing education in Norway, Tanzania and Malawi.

name: Linda Horne Mæland
summary: Linda Horne Mæland studies why nurses stay in their jobs and how they experience their working lives, with a focus on Norwegian school nurses, nursing home nurses and mental health nurses. Her work uses qualitative methods, including individual and focus group interviews analysed with phenomenological hermeneutic and thematic approaches, and draws on concepts such as self-realization, self-care and transformational leadership. The topics span nurse retention, professional values, leadership strategies of first-line nursing leaders and nurses' well-being in school health services, nursing homes and acute mental health wards.

name: Lise Sæstad Beyene
summary: Lise Sæstad Beyene studies mental healthcare practice, focusing on medication-free treatment, milieu therapy and the relationships between patients and professionals. She uses qualitative designs such as focus groups, interviews and case studies with thematic analysis, together with scoping and integrative reviews on relational competence and how it is taught in mental health education. Her work covers inpatient and community mental health settings in Norway, primary care group courses for depression, and the self-care of mental health nurses.

name: Magnus Jørgensen
summary: Magnus Jørgensen studies how life course transitions and socioeconomic background relate to mental health, using long-running Norwegian cohort data that follow people from adolescence into midlife. His work applies Bayesian structural equation models and regression analyses to examine the timing of parenthood, adolescent health behaviors, life satisfaction and depressive symptoms, with attention to gender differences and selection effects. The findings inform understanding of social inequalities in mental health and where prevention and early intervention could be directed in a Nordic welfare context.

name: Marianne Storm
summary: Marianne Storm studies digital health and nursing care, with a focus on self-management support for people with long-term conditions such as heart failure, colorectal cancer and serious mental illness. Her work combines qualitative interviews, co-creation and simulation methods, literature reviews, feasibility studies and randomised trial protocols to evaluate nurse-assisted remote monitoring, digital peer support and AI tools. Application areas include hospital-to-home transitions, community mental health and housing services, home healthcare for older adults, and the nursing workforce.

name: Marie Undheim
summary: Marie Undheim studies nursing education, with a focus on how blended learning is used to teach clinical skills to bachelor's nursing students at satellite campuses in Southern Norway. Her work uses a cross-sectional survey design, combining a validated satisfaction and self-confidence scale analysed with descriptive statistics and open-ended responses analysed through content analysis. The research addresses rural nursing workforce needs by examining how students experience decentralised, distance-supported skills training.

name: Marit Alstveit
summary: Marit Alstveit studies public health nursing, with a focus on postnatal care for new families and on public health nurse education. Her work uses qualitative methods, including phenomenological interviews with mothers and fathers, a meta-ethnography of nurses' perspectives, and a comparison of national legislation across the Nordic countries. It applies to child and family health centres, municipal postnatal services, and nursing education.

name: Marte Johanne Tangeraas Hansen
summary: Marte Johanne Tangeraas Hansen studies nursing practice in infection prevention and control, with a focus on antimicrobial resistance and antibiotic stewardship in hospitals. Her work uses qualitative methods, including repeated focus group interviews over several years, to examine how registered nurses' attitudes and confidence changed while caring for patients with multidrug-resistant bacteria before and during the COVID-19 pandemic. The application setting is hospital care in Norway.

name: Morten Munkvik
summary: Morten Munkvik's listed publications cover the use of artificial intelligence, with a 2026 piece framing it through a SMART approach, and the organisation of Norwegian primary care. A 2023 Norwegian-language article discusses how a patient-adjusted basic subsidy could affect the regular general practitioner (fastlege) scheme. The work appears to sit at the intersection of health services, health policy and digital technology.

name: Ole Tjomsland
summary: Ole Tjomsland studies health services and health system governance in Norway, with a focus on patient safety, quality measurement and unwarranted variation in clinical practice. His work combines registry-based cohort analysis, qualitative interviews with surgeons, policy framework development and protocols for intervention programmes that aim to reduce low-value procedures such as shoulder arthroscopy and upper endoscopy. It also covers hospital leadership tools such as clinical dashboards and the sustainable introduction of robotic surgery in public specialist healthcare.

name: Randi Wågø Aas
summary: Randi Wågø Aas studies how workplace and school environments relate to health, participation and absence, with a main focus on alcohol use among employees and sickness absence. Her work uses cross-sectional surveys, regression and multilevel modelling, a systematic review with meta-analysis, and qualitative interviews analysed with content analysis. Application areas include occupational health services, return to work after long-term sick leave, and pupils' risk of leaving upper secondary school.

name: Rosalynn Austin
summary: Rosalynn Austin researches heart failure care, with a focus on heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) services in the UK and on nurse-supported digital health for people with chronic illness. Her work uses scoping and systematic reviews, consensus surveys, mixed methods analyses and a randomised trial protocol to study service provision, remote patient monitoring, diet-focused mHealth apps and research recruitment. Other publications cover medication review in advanced kidney disease and sex and gender in cardiovascular research.

name: Stig Erlend Bjønness
summary: Stig Erlend Bjønness studies mental health services for young people and other vulnerable groups in Norway, with a focus on refugee, national minority, Indigenous and adolescent populations. His work uses qualitative interviews, systematic reviews and a mixed methods project protocol that includes a cohort and a randomized trial. It addresses access to care, user involvement and shared decision-making, culturally sensitive and digital services, and low-threshold support for people who use drugs.

name: Terese Elisabet Bondas
summary: Terese Elisabet Bondas studies maternal, child and family health, and the experiences of patients, families and health professionals in nursing and midwifery. She mainly uses meta-ethnography, a method for interpretive synthesis of qualitative studies, and also carries out primary qualitative studies using focus groups, interviews, and phenomenological, hermeneutic and visual approaches. Her topics include alcohol and substance use in families and pregnancy, refugee and immigrant care, LGBTQ+ parenthood, postnatal and public health nursing, nursing leadership, and the methodological development of meta-ethnography itself.

name: Thomas Westergren
summary: Thomas Westergren studies child and adolescent health, with a focus on public health nursing, well-child services and school health, and how families and nurses experience online screening tools. His work combines qualitative methods (observation, interviews, focus groups, reflexive thematic analysis) with evidence syntheses such as meta-ethnographies, scoping reviews and metasyntheses, plus a cross-sectional regression study of quality of life, mental health and socioeconomic status in young children. He also develops methods for qualitative longitudinal research and examines topics including parents' online health information seeking, very-low-birthweight infants' discharge, asthma and physical activity, inclusive arts, and transition to adult care.

name: Torgeir Gilje Lid
summary: Torgeir Gilje Lid studies alcohol use, opioid use and chronic pain, mainly in primary care and addiction treatment settings in Norway. His work combines randomized and pilot trials of lifestyle and treatment interventions (smoking cessation, nutrition, exercise, dextroamphetamine substitution, multidisciplinary pain care) with population survey, registry and prescribing-data analyses, as well as qualitative and implementation studies. Applications include screening and case finding for alcohol problems, care for people on opioid agonist therapy, and monitoring of opioid prescribing.

name: Trond Erik Grønnestad
summary: Trond Erik Grønnestad conducts qualitative research on health and social services for people who use drugs or have severe mental illness, mainly in Norway. His studies use interviews, focus groups and ethnographic fieldwork to examine public gathering places and open drug scenes, legal and human rights challenges in municipal services, and user and parent participation in adolescent inpatient mental healthcare. The work applies to harm reduction, low-threshold services, service coordination and policy in municipal and specialist care.

name: Unn Elisabeth Hammervold
summary: Unn Elisabeth Hammervold studies mental health and substance use care, focusing on supported housing and service organisation for people with co-occurring substance use and mental health problems, including recovery and health promotion in the Nordic context. Her work also covers how relational competence is taught in mental health education for healthcare professionals, and patients' experiences of post-incident reviews after restraint in acute psychiatric care. She uses scoping reviews with systematic database searches and thematic analysis, alongside qualitative interviews with patients.

name: Adriana Rosenberg
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Adriana Rosenberg studies patient safety and how healthcare safety investigators are trained. Her publication evaluates a master's level course in safety investigation for a national investigatory body in Norway, using individual and focus group interviews analysed with thematic analysis. The work informs the design of curricula for multidisciplinary investigators in health services.

name: Aina Lillian Bjerkeli Lekens
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Aina Lillian Bjerkeli Lekens studies how nurse anaesthetists understand and practise nursing care for surgical patients in the perioperative setting. Her work uses qualitative methods, including interviews with nurse anaesthetists in Norway analysed by content analysis and a meta-ethnographic synthesis of earlier qualitative studies. The findings address patient safety, person-centred care, professional competence and the education and supervision of nurse anaesthetists.

name: Anders Batman Mjelle
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Anders Batman Mjelle studies infections in newborns and children, focusing on bacterial meningitis and early-onset neonatal sepsis. His work uses retrospective review of hospital medical records and measurement of inflammatory markers such as C-reactive protein, analysed with descriptive and correlation statistics. The findings inform clinical diagnosis, antibiotic use and follow-up of neonates and children in paediatric and neonatal care.

name: Anita Salamonsen
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Anita Salamonsen studies mental health services and wellbeing for young people from refugee, Indigenous Sami, national minority and disability backgrounds, mainly in Norway. Her work combines qualitative interviews, systematic reviews, participatory action research and a mixed methods project with a cohort and randomized trial design. Application areas include culturally adapted care, youth involvement in treatment decisions, digital mental health services, and arts and music as routes to wellbeing.

name: Asma Sabri
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Asma Sabri studies person-centred practice in stroke care, looking at how patients experience care across the full course of recovery from onset through discharge and follow-up. Her work combines a qualitative interview study in Norway, using reflexive thematic analysis and patient journey mapping, with a scoping review of the international literature following JBI methodology. The findings address continuity of care, shared decision-making, rehabilitation access and the gap between standardised pathways and individual needs.

name: Ayyad Ahmad Zartasht Khan
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Ayyad Ahmad Zartasht Khan studies dry eye disease and the stability of the tear film, using clinical data from patients at a specialized dry eye clinic in Norway. The work applies retrospective analysis of standardized ocular surface examinations, with correlation and regression models, to test how age relates to fluorescein tear film break-up time. The findings inform clinical understanding of ocular surface disease and the factors behind tear film instability in symptomatic patients.

name: Birte Fagerdal
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Birte Fagerdal studies resilience in healthcare, with a focus on how hospital teams adapt to demand and resource pressures and how team, leadership, organizational and health-system factors shape that adaptive capacity. Her work mainly uses qualitative methods such as multiple case studies, observation, interviews, focus groups, stakeholder analysis and participatory workshops, including cross-country comparisons. She also develops and tests learning tools and principles for putting resilience theory into practice in hospitals, nursing homes and home care, and examines the role of champions and policy implications.

name: Bjørg Frøysland Oftedal
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Bjørg Frøysland Oftedal studies nursing and health professional practice, mainly through qualitative designs such as hermeneutic, discourse, content and thematic analysis based on interviews. Her work covers why Norwegian school nurses remain in practice, nurse and physician experiences of counselling and interprofessional follow-up for people at risk of type 2 diabetes in primary care, and how master's-level education shapes health professionals' understanding of health and competence. She has also contributed to a randomised controlled trial of a lifestyle intervention and to simulation-based newborn resuscitation training and quality improvement studies in a rural Tanzanian hospital.

name: Bodil Bø
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Bodil Bø studies simulation-based education in nursing and midwifery programmes, mainly in low-resource settings in Tanzania, Malawi and Madagascar. Her work combines qualitative studies, mixed-methods designs, a randomised controlled trial, a quasi-experimental study and a meta-synthesis to look at student experiences, knowledge and competence gains, and barriers to implementation. She also develops and psychometrically tests competence assessment tools, including perioperative and spiritual care scales, and has studied immigrants' experiences in Norway during COVID-19.

name: Britt S. Hansen
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Britt S. Hansen studies nursing practice, patient safety and professional education, with a focus on anaesthesia, perioperative and critical care nursing. Her work mainly uses qualitative interviews, focus groups, Delphi panels and evidence syntheses, alongside pre-post and mortality review evaluations of simulation training and rapid response systems. Application areas include competence assessment in postgraduate nursing placements, team training for stroke thrombectomy, deteriorating-patient systems, and cancer survivors' return to work.

name: Camilla Jacqueline Hansine Normand
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Camilla Jacqueline Hansine Normand studies how cardiac resynchronization therapy and other implantable cardiac devices are delivered to heart failure patients, focusing on differences between countries and patient groups. Her work uses large European surveys and registries, including cross-country comparisons of health spending and patient selection, along with external validation of a machine learning mortality risk score. She has also carried out a scoping review of educational supervision in internal medicine residency training.

name: Cecilie Haraldseid-Driftland
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Cecilie Haraldseid-Driftland studies resilience in healthcare, focusing on how organizations, leaders and staff adapt and sustain mental well-being in elderly care, home care, nursing homes and hospitals. Her work combines qualitative focus group and interview studies, systematic reviews, survey instrument development and validation, and participatory co-design of learning tools and frameworks. She also contributes to the Support4Resilience project, which develops a digital toolbox for leaders in older adult care across several countries.

name: Charity Atim Fabio Ambrose
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Charity Atim Fabio Ambrose studies how young people with refugee backgrounds from Central and East Africa experience mental health support in Norway's municipal health services. Her work uses qualitative methods, namely individual interviews with 16 youths analysed through thematic analysis. It looks at trust, confidentiality, cultural background, stigma, language barriers and discrimination as influences on access to care, with a view to improving culturally appropriate service delivery.

name: Clemens Weber
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Clemens Weber conducts clinical research in spine surgery and neurotrauma, with much of the work drawn from the multicentre NORDSTEN randomized trials on lumbar spinal stenosis and degenerative spondylolisthesis. These studies compare surgical approaches such as decompression with or without fusion and different decompression techniques, using patient-reported outcomes, MRI and radiographic measures, and follow-up of up to five years. He also studies trauma in older adults, including traumatic brain injury, low-energy falls, undertriage and odontoid fractures, using registry data and prospective cohorts, and has compared navigation methods for pedicle screw placement in spine fractures.

name: Dagrunn Nåden Dyrstad
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Dagrunn Nåden Dyrstad studies nursing and health professions education, with a focus on how competence is assessed in clinical placements for postgraduate critical care nursing students. Her work uses qualitative interviews, document analysis, and integrative and scoping reviews to examine the views of students, preceptors and teachers. She also investigates simulation-based training, including virtual simulation for clinical judgment, supervisor training, and interprofessional training in health needs assessment of older adults living at home.

name: Daniel Adrian Lungu
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Daniel Adrian Lungu studies the mental wellbeing and resilience of older adult care workers and informal caregivers, and how health risk information is communicated to the public, especially during the COVID-19 pandemic. His work uses qualitative interviews and focus groups, systematic reviews, randomized online experiments, regression analyses of survey data, and mixed-methods protocols. Application areas include long-term care policy, workplace burnout in care and academic settings, digital health apps, contraceptive prescribing and the validation of clinical questionnaires.

name: David Westfall Bates
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: David Westfall Bates studies patient safety and quality of care, covering adverse events from cancer immunotherapy as well as how healthcare systems and staff coped with the COVID-19 pandemic. His methods include retrospective multicentre cohort analysis, systematic review with qualitative meta-synthesis, focus group interviews, and comparative document analysis of regulatory policy. Application areas include oncology treatment safety, resilience in primary and nursing home care, and external inspection and accreditation of health services in Norway and the United States.

name: Eldar Søreide
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Eldar Søreide studies patient safety and healthcare quality in hospitals, alongside long-term outcomes after cardiac arrest. Work includes a multi-year follow-up of cardiac arrest survivors and their relatives, a mortality review of a rapid response system in gastrointestinal surgery, interviews with surgeons about reporting serious adverse events, and the development of a clinical dashboard to track unwarranted variation for hospital leaders. Methods span clinical trial follow-up, questionnaires, retrospective record review, qualitative interviews and quality indicator design, applied in Norwegian hospital settings.

name: Elin Espeland
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Elin Espeland studies digital learning in nursing education, with a focus on how students learn practical clinical skills. Her work uses an exploratory qualitative design, including focus group interviews analysed with qualitative content analysis, to examine second-year nursing students' experiences of an interactive skills training app. The findings relate to using mobile learning tools as a supplement to teacher-led clinical skill instruction.

name: Eline Ree
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Eline Ree studies resilience in healthcare, with a focus on how managers, leaders and staff champions support adaptive performance in hospitals, nursing homes, home care and long-term care systems across several countries. Her methods include qualitative interviews and case studies, systematic reviews, stakeholder analysis, comparative policy analysis, survey instrument development and validation, and co-designed intervention tools. She also researches the mental health, service experiences and help-seeking of refugee, minority and Indigenous youth in Norway, including digital mental health services.

name: Ellinor Haukland
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Ellinor Haukland conducts retrospective, real-world studies in clinical oncology, mainly using electronic health records, regional data and national registers, with survival analyses and regression models. The work covers palliative radiotherapy and prognostic scores, systemic therapy for prostate, kidney, lung and colon cancers, immune checkpoint inhibitors, brain metastases, and end-of-life care and work ability after cancer. Many studies come from rural northern Norway and assess patterns of care, treatment timing and patient selection.

name: Hans Morten Lossius
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Hans Morten Lossius studies prehospital emergency medicine, focusing on how emergency medical services deliver critical care and how that care can be improved. His publications use prospective observational multicentre and quasi-experimental interrupted time-series designs, covering airway management by anaesthetist-staffed helicopter and ambulance teams and educational training to improve vital sign monitoring in children. The work applies to emergency medical service practice and paediatric readiness in the Nordic countries.

name: Hege Langli Ersdal
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Hege Langli Ersdal's publications cover newborn resuscitation, maternal and newborn care quality in Tanzania and Ethiopia, and simulation-based training for clinicians. Her methods include a stepped-wedge cluster-randomized trial, prospective observational and video studies, cross-sectional surveys, qualitative interviews and cost-effectiveness analysis. Related work covers stroke thrombectomy access and training in Norway, and surgical training in appendicitis.

name: Helle Håve Stangeland
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Helle Håve Stangeland studies long-term cognitive outcomes after ischaemic stroke in working-age patients, using longitudinal MRI cohorts. Her work applies deep learning brain age estimation, mixed-effects and regression models, and voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping to examine brain aging, global cognition and emotion recognition years after stroke. She has also contributed commentary on epidemiological research linking childhood trauma to psychiatric disorders in young people.

name: Henriette Thune
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Henriette Thune studies how health risk information about pandemics is communicated to the public, using COVID-19 in Norway as the main case. Her work combines qualitative methods (expert and public interviews, thematic analysis, mental models) with a randomized controlled experiment testing how video features such as source and call to action affect trust, comprehension, intentions and behavior. It also looks at collaboration between health experts and creative communicators to design evidence-based video communication for the public and decision makers.

name: Hilda Bø Lyng
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Hilda Bø Lyng studies resilience in healthcare, with a focus on hospitals, nursing homes and aged and long-term care. Her work combines survey instrument development and validation, systematic reviews, document analysis, comparative cross-country policy analysis, case studies and participatory design of learning tools. It addresses workforce wellbeing, leadership, collaborative learning, patient safety and incident reporting, and the translation of resilience theory into practice.

name: Ingrid Tjoflåt
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Ingrid Tjoflåt studies nursing and midwifery education and practice, with a focus on simulation-based education for teaching clinical skills such as postpartum hemorrhage management in low-resource settings including Tanzania, Malawi and Madagascar. Her work uses qualitative, mixed-method, quasi-experimental, cross-sectional, Delphi and meta-synthesis designs to examine student learning, educator practices such as debriefing, and barriers to implementation. She also investigates perioperative nursing, including operating room nurses' non-technical skills and postoperative care in a conflict-affected hospital in Nigeria.

name: Ingvild Dalen
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Ingvild Dalen works on biostatistics and clinical epidemiology, with a focus on validating patient-reported outcome measures and diagnostic classification tools in orthopaedic settings such as ankle and hip fractures. Her publications use methods including confirmatory factor analysis, reliability and agreement studies, systematic reviews, trajectory modelling, multilevel regression and randomised trial protocols. Application areas include pregnancy-related pelvic and low back pain, dementia and depressive symptoms, eHealth after hospital discharge, older adult health assessment and alcohol use and sick leave in the workplace.

name: Ingvild Margreta Morken
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Ingvild Margreta Morken studies nurse-assisted eHealth and remote patient monitoring to support self-management and self-care in people with heart failure and colorectal cancer after hospital discharge. Her work combines qualitative interviews and observation, mixed methods analysis of usage data, literature reviews, and trial and feasibility protocols conducted at Norwegian university hospitals. She has also examined nurse-performed handheld ultrasound in a cardiac intensive care unit using an inter-rater agreement design.

name: Irene Sirevåg
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Irene Sirevåg researches the non-technical skills of operating room nurses, such as communication, teamwork, ethical competence and professional accountability, in the context of perioperative nursing and patient safety. Her work uses qualitative thematic analysis of expert nurse descriptions and Delphi panel methods with content validity indexing to develop and validate the NOTSORN behavioural marker tool. The tool is intended for supervision, self-reflection and education in operating room nursing.

name: Jeffrey Braithwaite
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Jeffrey Braithwaite studies resilience and workforce wellbeing in healthcare, with a focus on aged care and hospital staff. His work combines systematic and qualitative reviews, survey-based network and cluster analyses, mediation testing and staff interviews to examine how individual, organisational and system-level factors, including leadership, shape burnout, mental wellbeing and intention to leave. The findings are applied to workforce sustainability, care system design and policy recommendations for resilient health care.

name: Jo Røislien
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Jo Røislien works on biostatistics and health data analysis applied to prehospital and critical care, health communication and medical education. His publications use mathematical location optimization (such as maximum covering models) to plan helicopter and air-mobile stroke unit bases in Norway, alongside randomized experiments, quasi-experimental studies, protocols, and systematic, scoping and overview reviews. Other topics include remote and simulation-based training for clinicians, video communication during the COVID-19 pandemic, digital mental health services for minority youth, and reporting of data linkage in multimorbidity research.

name: Julian Thompson
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Julian Thompson studies how cognitive biases influence clinical decision-making in prehospital and in-hospital critical care. The work uses a scoping review following the Joanna Briggs Institute framework to map evidence across several medical databases. It catalogues the biases involved, the factors that contribute to them and the strategies proposed to reduce decision errors and patient harm in emergency medical settings.

name: Karina Aase
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Karina Aase studies how health and social care services work in practice, mainly in Norway, using qualitative, mixed methods, service design and scoping review approaches. Her work covers supported housing for adults with intellectual disabilities, care for children with cerebral palsy, stroke patient journeys, home care for older adults and ambulance services. Common threads are the experiences of service users, families, frontline staff and managers, along with care coordination, professional adaptation, patient safety and person-centred or family-centred care.

name: Kristin Akerjordet
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Kristin Akerjordet studies resilience and mental wellbeing among healthcare workers, informal caregivers and nursing students, with a focus on elderly and aged care and the role of leadership. She also researches nursing education, including co-creation with students, educators and mentors to design digital educational resources for clinical placements in nursing homes, as well as simulation feedback and emotional intelligence training. Her methods include systematic, scoping and qualitative reviews, interview and focus group studies, and a cross-country mixed-methods intervention project, plus a qualitative study of contraceptive counselling in Tanzania.

name: Kristin Alstveit Laugaland
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Kristin Alstveit Laugaland studies clinical education in nursing, focusing on first-year student nurses' placements in nursing homes and on mentorship, supervision and assessment practices. Her work uses qualitative methods such as interviews, focus groups, observation, phenomenological analysis and video-stimulated recall, along with a scoping review. She also examines co-creation and the design and evaluation of digital educational resources with students, nurse educators, nurse mentors and e-learning designers.

name: Kristin Glenna Bodsberg
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Kristin Glenna Bodsberg conducts qualitative research in nursing, spanning nursing education and the experiences of cancer patients. Her studies use focus group and individual interviews analyzed with content analysis to examine how nursing students and practicing nurses engage with digital learning tools such as a skills training app and student-made digital stories, and how women with breast cancer prepare to return to work during treatment. The work is relevant to nursing education, continuing professional development and supportive care in oncology and the workplace.

name: Kristin Tønsager
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Kristin Tønsager studies prehospital emergency medicine, focusing on out-of-hospital cardiac arrest and the care of injured patients before they reach hospital. Her work includes a multicentre randomised controlled trial across Norway, Denmark and Italy testing aortic balloon occlusion as an addition to advanced life support, and a prospective observational study of video streaming in emergency medical communication centres and its link to bystander first aid. The studies combine clinical trial and observational designs with regression analysis of outcomes such as return of spontaneous circulation and recognition of first aid needs.

name: Kristy Elizabeth Stohlmann
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Kristy Elizabeth Stohlmann studies how health-care workers, particularly nurses, learn and adapt while working, and how this learning supports resilient practice. Her work combines conceptual discussion of reflective and dialogic spaces in health-care systems with qualitative interview research, analysed thematically, on how experienced nurses move into new work practices. The findings are aimed at health-care organisations, nursing leaders, educators and policy makers working on professional development.

name: Lars Vatne Jacobsen
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Lars Vatne Jacobsen studies medical education with a focus on teaching point-of-care ultrasound to health professionals. The publication compares remote, videoconference-guided ultrasound training with classroom teaching in a group of 44 prehospital critical care students, using pre- and post-course tests of knowledge, image interpretation, scanning technique and clinical decision-making. The work applies to telemedicine and training in settings that require physical distancing or are geographically remote.

name: Lene Schibevaag
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Lene Schibevaag studies resilience in healthcare, including the capacities, adaptive processes and collaborative learning that help health systems maintain quality and safety. Her work relies mainly on qualitative methods such as interviews, grounded theory, narrative meta-synthesis, stakeholder analysis and participatory workshops. It is applied to Norwegian settings including nursing homes, home care and safety investigation training, and it feeds into learning tools and policy recommendations.

name: Malin Emilia Rosell Magerøy
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Malin Emilia Rosell Magerøy studies leadership, patient safety and staff safety in healthcare, with a focus on Norwegian nursing homes. Her work uses qualitative case studies based on interviews and focus groups with nursing home leaders, department leaders and elected politicians, and a literature review on work hours. It examines how leaders balance workplace health and safety with quality of care, and how regulation, organisational structure, relationships and shift patterns affect this.

name: Marcus Thomas Thor Roalsø
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Marcus Thomas Thor Roalsø studies surgical outcomes in pancreatic and liver cancer, using national registry data, population-based cohorts and multicenter observational studies to examine survival, recurrence, complications and sex differences after pancreatectomy and hepatectomy. He also carries out systematic reviews and meta-analyses on rare pancreatic conditions such as pancreatic metastases, mucinous cystic neoplasms and IPMN-related cancer. In addition, his work covers laboratory and translational topics, including patient-derived organoid models of pancreatic tumors, early detection biomarkers and cancer epigenetics.

name: Maria C. Gonzalez
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Maria C. Gonzalez studies dementia with Lewy bodies, Parkinson's disease and Parkinson's disease dementia, with a focus on biomarkers and disease progression. Her work uses multicenter cohort data, including plasma and cerebrospinal fluid markers, MRI measures, genetic variants and clinical assessments, analysed with longitudinal mixed-effects, survival and classification models. Applications include diagnosis, distinguishing Lewy body disease from Alzheimer's disease, prognosis of cognitive, motor and neuropsychiatric change, sex differences in brain atrophy, and the design of clinical trials.

name: Maria Nyre Vigmostad
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Maria Nyre Vigmostad's work in this publication concerns the diagnosis of prostate cancer, specifically how a blood-based risk test (Stockholm3) and magnetic resonance imaging can guide decisions about biopsy. It uses a real-life clinical cohort of several hundred men with a positive test but negative imaging, comparing the clinically significant and insignificant cancers found by systematic biopsy to estimate the effect of skipping biopsies. The findings apply to urology clinics and prostate cancer screening and diagnostic pathways, with the aim of reducing unnecessary biopsies and overdiagnosis.

name: Marius Rehn
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Marius Rehn works on emergency, pre-hospital and critical care medicine, with a focus on trauma, haemorrhage control, pain management and sedation. His publications include systematic reviews, scoping reviews and GRADE-based practice guidelines, along with endorsement reviews of guidelines for the Scandinavian anaesthesia and intensive care society using the AGREE II tool. He also designs experimental physiology studies, such as a crossover trial of supplemental oxygen during simulated blood loss in healthy volunteers.

name: Matthew Robert Hilditch
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Matthew Robert Hilditch conducts systematic reviews in prehospital and emergency medical services care. His work appraises the evidence on high-fidelity simulation training for critical care paramedics in aviation settings, and compares the FAST and BE-FAST screening tools for recognising acute stroke in the ambulance. The studies focus on paramedic education, patient safety and diagnostic accuracy in high-acuity emergencies.

name: Melissa Anne Elin Authen Weibell
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Melissa Anne Elin Authen Weibell studies severe mental illness, including schizophrenia, bipolar disorder and major depressive disorder, combining cognitive research with biological markers. Her work includes a meta-analysis of long-term cognitive change after psychosis onset, an epigenome-wide study of DNA methylation linked to birth complications, and large case-control studies of blood markers of immune activation, inflammation and gut barrier function. These studies draw on registry data, plasma and gene expression measurements, and stem cell-derived neurons.

name: Melissa Auten Weibell
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Melissa Auten Weibell studies the role of innate immune activity in severe mental illnesses, particularly schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. Using a large patient and healthy-control cohort, her work measures blood levels of IL-18 system proteins, inflammasome-related gene expression and lipid markers, and examines how cholesterol patterns relate to inflammation. The research aims to clarify inflammatory mechanisms in psychotic disorders and point to possible therapeutic targets.

name: Nils Petter Oveland
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Nils Petter Oveland works on point-of-care ultrasound and other bedside diagnostics for emergency and critical care, including consensus-based clinical recommendations for lung ultrasound and studies of ultrasound teaching. His research also covers experimental work in pigs, such as testing a microwave device to detect air and blood in the chest after trauma, and a report on fatal sepsis traced to contaminated propofol anaesthesia. Application areas include prehospital and emergency medicine, trauma care, telemedicine education and anaesthesia safety.

name: Nina Hjertvikrem
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology

name: Per Kristian Hyldmo
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Per Kristian Hyldmo studies prehospital and emergency care, with a focus on stroke thrombectomy access and training, trauma imaging, and clinical education. His work includes registry-based and before-after studies of stroke treatment, a phantom-based radiography study of spinal immobilization devices, and a comparison of remote and classroom ultrasound teaching. He also carries out systematic and scoping reviews on prehospital pain relief with opioids and inhaled agents, and on aeromedical retrieval services.

name: Peter Dieckmann
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology

name: Petter Viksveen
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Petter Viksveen studies health services research in Norway, focusing on mental health services for adolescents and for youth with refugee, minority and Indigenous backgrounds, and on home care and service design for older adults. His work uses qualitative interviews, workshops, co-research with adolescents, systematic reviews, mixed methods protocols and survey-based psychometric testing. Application areas include culturally sensitive and digital mental health services, user involvement and shared decision-making, patient safety culture, and resilience of care workers.

name: Philipp Seidel
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Philipp Seidel works on emergency and critical care medicine, covering early prediction of neurological outcome in comatose patients after cardiac arrest and point-of-care diagnosis of traumatic chest injuries. The cardiac arrest work is a prospective multicentre observational study combining head CT, EEG and a blood marker of brain injury (neurofilament light) to assess whether good or poor outcomes can be identified from 24 hours. The trauma work is an experimental pig study testing a microwave device with multiple antennas to detect air and blood in the chest cavity.

name: Runar Salte
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Runar Salte's listed work examines traumatic pneumothorax in civilian and military injury settings, separating simple pneumothorax from tension pneumothorax and comparing patients who breathe on their own with those on positive pressure ventilation. The publication is a position-style review that sets out definitions, pathophysiology, diagnosis and a standardized nomenclature. It also proposes treatment approaches that differ according to ventilation status, with relevance to emergency and trauma care.

name: S. E. Husebø
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: S. E. Husebø studies nursing education, with a focus on simulation-based learning, debriefing, facilitator and operator roles, clinical judgment and the teaching of practical nursing skills in simulation centres and clinical placements across Scandinavia. The work uses surveys, focus groups and interviews, quasi-experimental comparisons and scoping reviews. It also addresses clinical practice topics, including interprofessional team training and patient safety on surgical wards, person-centred stroke care, recovery and coping among cancer patients, surgical patient safety measurement and telemedicine for chronic wound care.

name: Sina Furnes Øyri
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Sina Furnes Øyri studies how external regulation, inspection and investigation shape quality, patient safety and resilience in healthcare and child welfare services, mainly in Norway. Her work uses qualitative interviews, document analysis, multilevel case studies, comparative policy review and meta-synthesis, involving regulators, hospital managers, surgeons and child welfare staff. Topics include learning from serious adverse events, stakeholder involvement in inspections, responses to supervisory findings and government pandemic response.

name: Siren Irene Rettedal
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Siren Irene Rettedal studies newborn and preterm infant care, including immediate skin-to-skin contact after very preterm birth and its effects on infant stress, neurodevelopment and parental mental health, using randomised trials and a systematic review. Her work also covers newborn resuscitation and birth asphyxia, using observational and video studies, heart rate monitoring and AI-based thermal and video analysis. She additionally examines neonatal care in Ethiopia and Tanzania through facility readiness assessments, implementation trial design and qualitative studies, and has reported on a neonatal unit infection outbreak.

name: Siri Lerstøl Olsen
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Siri Lerstøl Olsen studies patient safety and care of acutely ill and deteriorating hospital patients, including delirium in older adults in emergency departments and rapid response systems on hospital wards. Her work uses a scoping review, a retrospective interprofessional mortality review with statistical comparison across time periods, and qualitative system probing with in situ simulation and focus groups. The topics covered include detecting and preventing delirium, reducing omission events, and improving interprofessional collaboration and training in acute care.

name: Siri Wiig
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Siri Wiig studies resilience, quality and patient safety in healthcare, with a strong focus on elderly care, home care and aged care workforces. Her work uses qualitative interviews, systematic and scoping reviews, comparative policy analysis and survey instrument development and validation, and also covers leadership, regulation and mental well-being of staff. The research addresses how individuals, organisations and wider health systems adapt under pressure such as workforce shortages and crises.

name: Siv Hilde Berg
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Siv Hilde Berg studies mental health care and health and risk communication, with a focus on adolescents, patients at risk of suicide and minority youth in Norway. Her work uses systematic and scoping reviews, qualitative interviews, mixed methods designs, surveys and randomized experiments. Applications include resilient practice and patient safety in inpatient care, user involvement and digital services in youth mental health, public trust in government, and pandemic video communication.

name: Soffien Chadli Ajmi
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Soffien Chadli Ajmi studies how team-based simulation training and quality improvement work affect acute stroke care, covering both intravenous thrombolysis and endovascular thrombectomy. Using prospective cohort, pre-post intervention and economic evaluation methods, the work examines treatment times, patient outcomes, safety effects such as treatment of stroke mimics, the role of clinician experience, and anaesthetic management. The research is set in hospital stroke centres and relates to training of multidisciplinary treatment teams.

name: Solveig Hodne
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Solveig Hodne studies healthcare quality and patient safety in Norway, using nationwide registry-based analyses of malpractice and compensation claims for pancreatic cancer and acute pancreatitis. These studies examine claim rates, who the claims are directed at, how often they are approved, and the compensation paid, with delayed diagnosis and treatment errors as main themes. She is also involved in a mixed methods project on digital mental health services for national minority, Indigenous (Sámi) and refugee youth, combining a longitudinal survey cohort, interviews, co-development with youth and professionals, and a randomized trial.

name: Stephen Johan Mikal Sollid
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Stephen Johan Mikal Sollid studies prehospital and emergency medical services, with a focus on patient safety, quality improvement and team performance in ambulance and helicopter services. His work uses quasi-experimental and registry-based cohort designs, qualitative interviews and focus groups, consensus methods, surveys and scoping reviews. Application areas include medication errors, dispatch prioritisation and trauma systems, advanced airway management, rescue operations, ethical issues such as coercion, and patient experiences of stroke care in Norway and Switzerland.

name: Teklay Tesfay Kidanemariam
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Teklay Tesfay Kidanemariam studies resilience and mental well-being among health care professionals in home care and elderly care. The work uses qualitative methods, including focus group interviews with staff in Norwegian municipalities analysed thematically, within a resilience-in-healthcare framework. It examines how teamwork, leadership support, work organisation and individual coping strategies help staff perform under pressure.

name: Thor Ole Gulsrud
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Thor Ole Gulsrud works on digital histopathology for marine aquaculture health, developing automated image analysis of whole-slide histology to measure bacterial infection in farmed shellfish. His work on Vibrio aestuarianus in Pacific oysters uses immunohistochemical staining to calculate the share of infected tissue and describe how bacteria are spatially distributed, and compares the results with qPCR measurements. The application focus is early disease detection and monitoring in bivalve aquaculture.

name: Tone Knutsen Brandeggen
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Tone Knutsen Brandeggen studies digital teaching and learning methods in nursing education, including an interactive skills training app, virtual simulation software and digital storytelling. Her work uses exploratory qualitative designs, mainly focus group interviews analysed with content analysis, and draws on both nursing students' and practising clinical nurses' experiences. The application areas are clinical skill training, development of clinical judgment and reflective learning in hospital and nursing home settings.

name: Tor Paaske Utheim
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Tor Paaske Utheim works on dry eye disease and meibomian gland dysfunction, combining clinical cohort studies from a Norwegian dry eye clinic with systematic reviews and meta-analyses. His work covers symptom and tear film risk factors, treatments such as artificial tears, corticosteroids, hot towels, intense pulsed light, low-level light therapy and stem cell approaches, and ocular effects of glaucoma drops and refractive surgery. He also reviews scar minimization in oculoplastic surgery (brow lift, blepharoplasty, dacryocystorhinostomy) and has reported a case of traumatic globe dislocation.

name: Torunn Strømme
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Torunn Strømme studies how quality improvement and patient safety interventions are implemented in Norwegian nursing homes and home care services, and how nursing students learn clinical skills. Her work relies mainly on qualitative methods such as interviews, focus groups, participant observation and grounded theory, including multiple case studies of leadership and competence programmes. Topics include barriers and enablers to implementation, knowledge boundaries, recognition of deterioration in frail older patients, and the use of an interactive app in nursing education.

name: Vegard Asgeir Forsaa
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Vegard Asgeir Forsaa works in clinical ophthalmology, focusing on vitreoretinal surgery and diseases such as rhegmatogenous retinal detachment and macular hole. His studies combine prospective observational work, a randomized trial, a Delphi consensus study and imaging methods (OCT, infrared scanning laser ophthalmoscopy) to assess surgical technique, tamponade choice, postoperative recovery and retinal and choroidal changes. He also studies how repeated anti-VEGF intravitreal injections with povidone-iodine antisepsis affect the ocular surface, meibomian glands and tear cytokines, and has evaluated wet-lab training for open-globe injury management.

name: Veslemøy Guise
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Veslemøy Guise studies resilience in healthcare, focusing on how patients, families, informal caregivers, staff, leaders and other stakeholders contribute to adaptive, high-quality care. Her work uses qualitative methods such as interviews, focus groups, observation and stakeholder analysis, alongside systematic and narrative reviews and a mixed-methods study protocol, and develops frameworks and toolboxes for putting resilience theory into practice. Application areas include elderly and older adult care, hospital teams, integrated care for children with cerebral palsy, and transitional care for young adults with type 1 diabetes.

name: Victoria Vatsvåg
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Victoria Vatsvåg studies medical education in point-of-care ultrasound, focusing on whether teaching delivered remotely through videoconferencing can match in-person instruction. Her work compares student groups in a prehospital critical care program using pre- and post-course tests of knowledge, image interpretation, scanning technique and clinical decision-making. The findings relate to telemedicine and training in settings with physical distancing or long distances.

name: Vilde M. Thomseth
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Vilde M. Thomseth studies the retina and ocular surface in clinical ophthalmology, focusing on how repeated anti-VEGF intravitreal injections for neovascular age-related macular degeneration affect tear film, meibomian glands, redness and tear cytokines, and on recovery after rhegmatogenous retinal detachment surgery. Her work uses prospective and retrospective observational designs, with the fellow eye as control, along with imaging such as swept-source and en face optical coherence tomography, infrared homography and keratography, plus visual function testing and tear assays. She also reports on the long-term incidence of retinal detachment in Western Norway and on retinal and choroidal changes after reattachment.

name: Wolfgang George Cornelius Voelckel
department: Department of Quality and Health Technology
summary: Wolfgang George Cornelius Voelckel studies prehospital emergency and trauma medicine, with a focus on out-of-hospital cardiac arrest epidemiology and survival in adults and children treated by physician-staffed ground and helicopter services in Austria. His work uses retrospective and prospective cohort designs, registry and mission-record data, multivariable analyses and evidence reviews. It also covers trauma care topics including vasopressin in hemorrhagic shock, drugs for traumatic brain injury, the S100B biomarker in major trauma, and inhaled methoxyflurane for prehospital pain relief.

name: Anders Blilie
department: Faculty of Health Sciences (department not stated)
summary: Anders Blilie develops and validates deep learning systems for digital pathology of prostate cancer, covering diagnosis, Gleason grading and detection of cribriform morphology in whole-slide images of biopsies. The work tests how well these models hold up across laboratories, scanners and populations, including a Middle Eastern cohort, and examines technical factors such as tissue detection, scanner colour calibration and conformal prediction for flagging unreliable outputs. Further publications cover a public biopsy image dataset, a pre-registered validation protocol, AI use to reduce immunohistochemistry staining, and biobanking protocols for prostatectomy tissue.

name: Caroline Guldberg Fugelli
department: Faculty of Health Sciences (department not stated)
summary: Caroline Guldberg Fugelli studies how multidisciplinary simulation training affects care for acute stroke patients undergoing endovascular thrombectomy, with a focus on anaesthesia in non-operating room settings. Her work combines pre-post interventional studies of clinical workflow, anaesthetic management and patient outcomes with a qualitative focus group study of team members' training experiences. The research is applied in hospital stroke care and informs how simulation programmes and faculty are designed.

name: Frederikke Buskov
department: Faculty of Health Sciences (department not stated)
summary: Frederikke Buskov studies newborn transition and resuscitation in the delivery room, using prospective observational cohorts, video recording and dry-electrode ECG heart rate monitoring at a Norwegian university hospital. Her work examines how umbilical arterial pH, heart rate, Apgar scores, tactile stimulation and positive pressure ventilation relate to one another in birth asphyxia. She has also analysed selection bias in a randomized trial of newborn resuscitation that relied on video data.

name: Hanne Pike
department: Faculty of Health Sciences (department not stated)
summary: Hanne Pike studies newborn and preterm infant care, combining randomised clinical trials of immediate parent–infant skin-to-skin contact after very preterm birth with observational and video-based studies of delivery-room resuscitation.
