summary: Hans Joakim Skadsem studies well construction and well integrity, covering casing centralization, cement sealing and bonding, microannulus leakage and repair, and gas migration along wells. His work combines laboratory and full-scale experiments with finite element, CFD (OpenFOAM) and two-fluid modelling to examine cement and plug behaviour, fluid displacement in annuli and Hele-Shaw cells, and rheology of cement slurries. Applications include primary and reverse cementing, plug and abandonment, drill string and bearing flows, and sustained casing pressure.

name: Helleik Rosenvinge Syse
summary: Helleik Rosenvinge Syse studies energy use in buildings in Norway, combining day-ahead load forecasting, building performance simulation and comparisons of calculated versus measured energy. The work tests how forecast accuracy affects the cost savings from scheduling storage and electric vehicles in student housing, how certificate-based calculations differ from sub-metered data in municipal buildings, and how occupant behaviour is represented in simulation of a container-based energy lab. He also examines the barriers researchers face in obtaining consumer energy data from energy companies.

name: Hibat Errahmen Djecta
summary: Hibat Errahmen Djecta works on geosteering, the real-time steering of wells through uncertain subsurface geology, using machine learning and probabilistic methods. The publications combine particle filters, ensemble data assimilation and generative adversarial networks for uncertainty modeling with reinforcement learning and dynamic programming for sequential steering decisions. Work includes validation against an industrial geosteering simulator, an open benchmark on probabilistic forecasting of geological layers, and an interactive web demonstration for human-AI decision support.

name: Homam Nikpey Somehsaraei
summary: Homam Nikpey Somehsaraei works on modelling, simulation and optimization of energy systems, with a main focus on micro-gas turbines (including humidified and hydrogen-fuelled cycles) and on heat pumps, thermal storage and building energy use. His methods include physics-based and grey-box dynamic models, Modelica simulation, Taguchi and multi-objective optimization, and neural networks for condition monitoring and data denoising. Application areas include distributed power and heat generation, solar-assisted CO2 ground-source heating, phase change material cooling for residential buildings, and comparison of calculated and measured energy in municipal buildings.

name: Ivan Dario Pinerez Torrijos
summary: Ivan Dario Pinerez Torrijos studies enhanced oil recovery through Smart Water injection, tailoring brine chemistry to alter rock wettability in chalk, limestone and sandstone reservoirs. The work uses laboratory core experiments such as spontaneous imbibition and flooding, supported by surface and chemical analysis and geochemical simulation. It also examines how carbonated water interacts with reservoir and caprock minerals for CO2 storage, and how core restoration methods affect wettability reproducibility.

name: J. A. Aasen
summary: J. A. Aasen works on well integrity and barrier materials for oil and gas wells, covering both casing mechanics and cementitious sealing materials. The publications combine analytical stress calculations for oval, hydrogen-embrittled casing with laboratory tests of geopolymers and expansive additives, and characterization of aged field cement, using shear and hydraulic bond strength, expansion, calorimetry, microscopy and diffraction. The applications are zonal isolation, plugging and abandonment, and sour-service casing design in wells such as those on the Norwegian continental shelf.

name: J. Djuve
summary: J. Djuve's work addresses the use of rock-based geopolymers as a replacement for cement in oil and gas well construction. The publication describes designing and testing spacer fluids by tuning rheology with additives and surfactants, then measuring rheological compatibility, strength and heat evolution when the spacer and geopolymer mix. The work applies to mud displacement, zonal isolation and wellbore integrity.

name: Jassem Abbasi
summary: Jassem Abbasi studies multiphase flow in porous media, such as geological reservoir rocks, using physics-informed neural networks, numerical simulation and machine learning. The work covers forward and inverse modeling, history-matching of core-scale experiments (spontaneous imbibition, porous plate and centrifuge capillary pressure tests, fractured shale), and benchmarking of methods for shock and discontinuity handling. Applications include CO2 storage, hydrocarbon recovery, special core analysis, and permeability prediction for tight sandstones.

name: Jelena Popovic-Neuber
summary: Jelena Popovic-Neuber studies electrochemical energy storage, focusing on solid and liquid battery electrolytes, alkali, magnesium and aluminum metal electrodes, and silicon anodes. Her work uses electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and galvanostatic polarization in symmetric cells, alongside materials synthesis and mathematical modeling, to measure ion transport, interphase properties and effective cationic transference numbers. Application areas include solid-state, potassium, sodium and post-lithium batteries, polymer electrolytes and cation-conducting binders, with reviews and roadmap articles on the field.

name: Jonas Grill
summary: Jonas Grill studies ion transport and interphase behavior in battery materials, covering alkali metal, silicon, magnesium and aluminum electrodes in contact with liquid electrolytes, as well as polymer and inorganic solid-state electrolytes. The work relies mainly on electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, galvanostatic polarization and numerical modeling to determine quantities such as activation energies, charge transfer resistance, diffusion coefficients and cationic transference numbers. It supports the development of lithium, sodium, potassium and multivalent batteries, including solid-state cells and cation-conducting binders.

name: K. Gjerstad
summary: K. Gjerstad works on drilling fluid behavior and wellbore hydraulics, with a focus on real-time monitoring and digital twin applications in oil and gas wells. The publications combine physics-based and transient modeling, rheometer experiments on thixotropic muds, fast polynomial density models for high-pressure, high-temperature wells, and use of along-string pressure measurements to estimate cuttings in the mud. Application areas include hole cleaning, gel breaking and pressure surges at pump startup, and the effect of sea heave on tripping operations.

name: Kaan Kizmaz
summary: Kaan Kizmaz studies the electrochemical behavior of alkali metal electrodes (lithium, sodium and potassium) in contact with liquid battery electrolytes. Using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and galvanostatic polarization in symmetric cells, the work examines interphase layers, charge transfer, diffusion and cation transference as they change with time, temperature and concentration. The work also reviews these methods as non-destructive tools for assessing the stability and degradation kinetics of metal anodes in next-generation high energy density batteries.

name: Kasra Saberi Beglar
summary: Kasra Saberi Beglar works on the operation and control of multi-energy systems, covering deep reinforcement learning, load forecasting and optimization-based pricing. The publications include a structured literature review of reinforcement learning for energy management, a data-driven study of day-ahead forecasting and storage-based flexibility using data from a Norwegian student dormitory, and a bi-level optimization model for dynamic pricing between energy providers and consumers. Application areas are building and urban energy management, demand response, electric vehicle and battery scheduling, and tariff design.

name: Kate Lorna Powell
summary: Kate Lorna Powell studies sediment provenance and depositional systems in ancient continental basins, with a focus on the Permian Rotliegend Group of the Norwegian North Sea. Her work combines detrital zircon U–Pb geochronology, facies analysis, palaeocurrent data from wells and palinspastic restoration to trace sediment sources, transport pathways and tectonic influences. The results are applied to understanding how sediment origin affects reservoir quality and to predicting reservoir distribution in subsurface energy-related settings.

name: Kim Andre Nesse Vorland
summary: Kim Andre Nesse Vorland works on recovering critical metals from spent lithium-ion batteries and on geological carbon storage. His publications cover laboratory leaching of black mass with citric acid and choline chloride deep eutectic solvents, including optimisation of process conditions and measurement of viscosity and pH. They also include core-scale experiments on how CO2 exposure changes porosity and permeability in Danish chalk, relevant to the feasibility of storing CO2 in carbonate reservoirs.

name: Kjell Kåre Fjelde
summary: Kjell Kåre Fjelde works on gas behavior in oil and gas wells, studying how gas moves, expands and builds pressure during well control and drilling operations. His work combines drift-flux transient simulation, analytical models and laboratory flow-loop experiments, covering bullheading, kick migration in closed wells and gas unloading from marine risers. The studies address safety and equipment integrity questions in well kill, managed pressure drilling and offshore drilling.

name: Lucas Volpi
summary: Lucas Volpi studies how drilling fluid interacts with vibrating drill-strings, using coupled fluid–structure simulations. The work solves the fluid flow with the lattice-Boltzmann method, including Newtonian and non-Newtonian fluids, and couples it to finite element models of the drill-string to estimate hydraulic forces and torques on tool-joints. Results are compared with reduced-order force models to assess where simplified descriptions hold, for application to drilling operations.

name: Mahmood Fani
summary: Mahmood Fani studies how CO2 and carbonated water interact with reservoir rocks and fluids, with a focus on carbon capture, utilization and storage and on enhanced oil recovery. The work combines laboratory methods such as core flooding, spontaneous imbibition, mineral exposure tests with SEM, EDX and ion chromatography, and geochemical and wellbore simulation (PHREEQC, Eclipse E300). Application areas include sandstone and chalk reservoirs, caprock and storage integrity, CO2 injection operations such as Northern Lights, and microfluidic pore-scale study of chemical oil recovery.

name: Mahmoud Khalifeh
summary: Mahmoud Khalifeh's research centres on well integrity and sealing materials for oil and gas wells, plug and abandonment, and geological CO2 storage. Using laboratory testing (hydraulic sealability, rheology, mechanical and triaxial tests, microstructural analysis) together with pore-scale numerical and thermodynamic modeling, the publications examine rock-based geopolymers, stacked annular cement, remedial treatment fluids and drilling fluid stability. Related work covers low-carbon cement binders using industrial by-products, regulatory reviews of well abandonment and methane seepage, and leaching of metals from lithium-ion battery black mass using deep eutectic solvents.

name: Mesfin Belayneh Agonafir
summary: Mesfin Belayneh Agonafir studies well control and two-phase flow in drilling, focusing on how pressure builds up in a closed well when a gas kick migrates upward. The work develops a simplified analytical model and checks it against two transient drift-flux simulators, showing how kick size, well volume and liquid compressibility shape the pressure response. The findings apply to managed pressure drilling and conventional well control operations.

name: Mohammad Mansouri
summary: Mohammad Mansouri studies multi-energy and decentralized energy systems, covering optimization, scheduling, techno-economic and risk analysis, and reviews of deep reinforcement learning for system control. The work also covers hydrogen-fueled micro gas turbines, using physics-based performance models with machine learning for fault diagnosis and remaining-life estimation, as well as building-level flexibility, load forecasting, phase change material cooling, distribution network reconfiguration and biogas economics. Application areas include urban and island energy systems, residential buildings, hospital energy supply and rural bioenergy.

name: Mohsen Assadi
summary: Mohsen Assadi's publications cover decentralized and low-carbon energy systems, including hydrogen-fuelled micro gas turbines, electrolyzer and fuel cell systems with battery storage, and microgrid scheduling. They also cover shallow and deep geothermal systems such as borehole heat exchangers, thermal response tests and reuse of abandoned oil and gas wells. Methods include techno-economic and Monte Carlo risk analysis, mixed-integer and heuristic optimization, neural-network and digital twin models, CFD simulation, and field and laboratory measurements, applied to buildings, refineries, distribution grids, households and wave energy converters.

name: Mojtaba Ghaedi
summary: Mojtaba Ghaedi studies subsurface storage of hydrogen and CO2 in porous formations, salt caverns and caprocks, together with geothermal well scaling. His work combines analytical formulations, geochemical modeling with PHREEQC, reservoir simulation and optimization, and laboratory diffusion measurements. The studies address leakage and capillary sealing, diffusion and density-driven mixing, mineral reactions, salt precipitation, gas recovery, and techno-economic planning, often using field cases such as Norne, Ketzin and Northern Lights.

name: Mostafa Mohammadi
summary: Mostafa Mohammadi studies the quality of pre-drill forecasts used in petroleum exploration, covering both geological probability of success and prospect volume estimates. Using historical prospect data from the Norwegian Continental Shelf, the work applies forecast verification measures such as the Brier score, skill score and reliability diagrams to detect bias, overconfidence and miscalibration. It also develops simple calibration approaches, including reference class benchmarks and distribution adjustments, to improve exploration decision-making and portfolio evaluation.

name: Nestor Cardozo
summary: Nestor Cardozo works on subsurface geoscience, combining seismic interpretation, well-log analysis, structural and numerical modelling, and machine learning to characterize faults, salt structures and reservoirs. His studies, largely in the Norwegian North Sea and Barents Sea, cover seismic inversion, salt cavern suitability for hydrogen storage, geothermal thermal modelling, fault and fracture prediction, and ensemble-based structural model building. He also statistically evaluates petroleum exploration volume and probability forecasts, studies seismic attenuation linked to fault fluids in Colombia, and develops discrete element software for tectonic deformation.

name: Nisar Ahmed
summary: Nisar Ahmed works on quantitative seismic inversion for subsurface characterization, developing pre-stack and amplitude-versus-offset methods that use adjoint-state gradients and quasi-Newton optimization to estimate elastic properties, attenuation, and time-lapse saturation and pressure changes. He also compares these physics-based approaches with deep learning models such as convolutional and transformer networks, using field data from the North Sea including the Troll, Edvard Grieg and Smeaheia areas. Additional work covers seismic facies analysis of the Indus fan turbidite system and well-log-based geomechanics and pore pressure studies of Eocene reservoirs in South Asia.

name: Pål Østebø Andersen
summary: Pål Østebø Andersen studies multiphase flow in porous media, combining numerical and analytical modeling with physics-informed neural networks for history matching and inverse problems. His work covers spontaneous imbibition, saturation functions, fractured rock and capillary pressure testing, and extends to underground hydrogen storage, CO2-enhanced oil recovery, aquifer thermal energy storage and geothermal tracers. Applications use reservoir simulation, including the Norne field model, along with optimization and uncertainty analysis for storage design and subsurface energy operations.

name: Qian Zhang
summary: Qian Zhang studies thermal energy systems for buildings, including CO2 heat pumps, solar-assisted ground-source heating, borehole thermal storage and phase change material cooling. The work uses Modelica simulation, Taguchi and grey relational optimization, techno-economic analysis, and deep learning models for forecasting and control, plus CFD-style analysis of rotating flows in flywheel energy storage systems. Applications include space and water heating in cold climates, district heating, residential cooling, geothermal borehole performance prediction and flywheel thermal management.

name: R. G. Hanea
summary: R. G. Hanea works on ensemble-based methods for decision making under uncertainty in subsurface reservoir management. The publication uses the EVEREST optimization tool and an approximate gradient (StoSAG) as a sensitivity measure to rank which geological and operational uncertainties most affect field-development and well-planning decisions. The approach is demonstrated on a synthetic reservoir model (REEK) for oil and gas applications.

name: R. I. Korsnes
summary: R. I. Korsnes studies the mechanical and geochemical behavior of subsurface rocks and wellbore materials using laboratory triaxial testing, core flooding, and microscopy and diffraction analysis. The work covers chalk and carbonate reservoirs (brine-rock reactions, mineral precipitation, water weakening, temperature cycling, and chemical strengthening for fracturing), creep behavior of impure Zechstein salt for hydrogen storage caverns, and granite-based geopolymers as sealing materials for wells. Applications include improved oil recovery, CO2 and hydrogen storage, geothermal wells, and wellbore integrity.

name: Raoof Gholami
summary: Raoof Gholami studies subsurface energy and storage systems, with a strong focus on underground hydrogen storage, CO2 storage and geothermal energy. His work combines numerical and geochemical modelling (including PHREEQC), mathematical formulations, laboratory diffusion and rock mechanics tests, and analysis of real plant data. Topics include caprock sealing and leakage risk, salt cavern behaviour, density-driven flow, mineral reactions and hydrogen loss, calcite scaling in geothermal wells, and borehole heat exchanger design and performance.

name: Reidar B. Bratvold
summary: Reidar B. Bratvold works on decision analysis for subsurface energy projects, with a strong focus on geosteering, where drilling trajectories are adjusted sequentially under uncertainty. His methods include reinforcement learning, particle filters, approximate dynamic programming, deep neural networks, Bayesian optimization and real options valuation, as well as statistical studies of expert behavior and of forecast calibration. Applications include well placement, reservoir production optimization, petroleum exploration forecasting on the Norwegian Continental Shelf, energy transition investments such as offshore wind, and multi-criteria decision frameworks.

name: Rune Wiggo Time
summary: Rune Wiggo Time works on fluid mechanics, combining optical measurement of liquid properties with numerical simulation of multiphase and fluid–structure flows. His publications develop and validate a laser-sheet imaging method that uses capillary–gravity waves and inverse ray-tracing to estimate interfacial tension and viscosity, and compare Volume of Fluid and Level Set simulations of capillary waves. He also applies lattice-Boltzmann and finite element models to estimate hydraulic forces and vibrations on drill-strings and tool-joints in Newtonian and non-Newtonian drilling fluids.

name: Sadegh Ahmadpour

position.nb: Stipendiat i hydrogen lagring i porøse medier

summary: Sadegh Ahmadpour studies fluid flow and geochemical processes in porous subsurface formations, focusing on underground hydrogen storage and geological CO2 storage. The work combines mathematical formulations, numerical and reactive transport modelling (PHREEQC), and laboratory pressure-decay diffusion measurements to examine hydrogen loss, H2S formation, density-driven convection and gas diffusion in water and brine. Earlier work extends multiphase flow theory by deriving relative permeabilities from momentum equations with Brinkmann terms for core flooding and spontaneous imbibition.

name: Seyed Hasan Hajiabadi
summary: Seyed Hasan Hajiabadi studies granite-based geopolymers as alternatives to Portland cement for sealing wellbores in geological CO2 storage. The work combines laboratory testing under simulated downhole pressure and temperature (triaxial, coreflooding, permeability, microscopy, spectroscopy and diffraction) with pore-scale reaction-transport modeling of carbonation, and also includes a literature review and an assessment of cement testing standards. It examines slurry design, mechanical performance, and durability under exposure to CO2, CO2-saturated water and brines.

name: Siv Marie Åsen
summary: Siv Marie Åsen studies how thermo-thickening associative polymers flow through porous rock for enhanced oil recovery. Using laboratory flow experiments in sandstone and sand, the work measures how the resistance factor (mobility reduction) changes with associative content, salinity, temperature, flow velocity, time and sample size. The findings relate to polymer injectivity and sweep efficiency in oil reservoirs.

name: Skule Strand
summary: Skule Strand's publications address enhanced oil recovery and CO2 storage in porous reservoir rocks such as chalk, limestone, sandstone and diatomite. Using laboratory methods including spontaneous imbibition, core flooding, mineral-brine reactivity tests, microscopy and geochemical modelling, the work studies wettability alteration with tailored Smart Water brines, polysulphate additives, ionic liquids and carbonated water. Applications include North Sea chalk fields, produced water reuse, and the integrity of reservoir and caprock minerals during CO2 injection.

name: Slawosz Adrian Kleszcz
summary: Slawosz Adrian Kleszcz studies the economics of small-scale combined heat and power systems driven by micro gas turbines, running on natural gas and natural gas–hydrogen blends. The work combines experiments on a 3 kW turbine, process simulation in IPSEPro and cost modelling to calculate the levelized cost of electricity over a 20-year lifespan. Monte-Carlo simulation is used to assess risk and uncertainty, and the results are compared with grid electricity prices in a Norwegian case study.

name: Steinar Evje
summary: Steinar Evje works on mathematical modeling and numerical methods for partial differential equations, with a recent focus on learning unknown flux and diffusion functions of nonlinear conservation laws from observed data. His methods combine symbolic neural networks with entropy-satisfying discrete schemes, and also use Bayesian inversion with ensemble Kalman filters. He applies these to multiphase flow, gas leakage along wells in CO2 storage settings, and continuum models of tumor progression and interstitial fluid pressure in cancer.

name: Sverre Ekrene Ohm
summary: Sverre Ekrene Ohm studies petroleum geochemistry and source rocks on the Norwegian Continental Shelf, including North Sea and Barents Sea basins. The work combines organic petrography, Rock-Eval, stable carbon isotopes, biomarkers and trace-metal analysis of core samples and oils to interpret depositional environment, organofacies and oil origin, and also includes seafloor mapping and seismic interpretation of methane-emitting mud volcanoes in the Barents Sea.

name: Tina Puntervold
summary: Tina Puntervold studies how rock, brine and oil interact in carbonate, sandstone and diatomite reservoirs, focusing on wettability alteration for enhanced oil recovery. Her laboratory work uses spontaneous imbibition and core flooding, mineral and pore characterization (SEM/EDX, XRD, mercury intrusion, ion chromatography) and geochemical modelling with PHREEQC. Applications include Smart Water and additive-modified brines, produced water reinjection, nanoparticles and ionic liquids, outcrop versus reservoir rock analogues, and CO2-rich water for oil recovery and CO2 storage.

name: Tomasz Adam Skrzydlo
summary: Tomasz Adam Skrzydlo studies heterogeneous catalysis over silver, focusing on the sub-reactions involved in the industrial conversion of methanol to formaldehyde. Using an annular structured reactor and repeated scanning electron microscopy imaging, the work links CO and hydrogen oxidation activity to changes in catalyst surface structure under different gas mixtures and steam levels. The findings help separate the effects of temperature and feed composition on silver restructuring and clarify reaction pathways in formaldehyde production.

name: V. N. Lima
summary: V. N. Lima studies the integrity of cement-based barriers in oil and gas wells, using laboratory and full-scale experiments on cement sheaths, microannuli and cement-rock interfaces. The work combines single- and two-phase seepage and tracer tests, triaxial and shear bond strength testing, and rheological and chemical characterization of cement slurries and pastes, including exposure to H2S and CO2 and evaluation of resin sealants and additives. Related work covers fiber-reinforced concrete under cyclic loading, and the same experimental approach is applied to well leakage, zonal isolation and sustained casing pressure.

name: Veronika Abdulina
summary: Veronika Abdulina studies how mineralogy, pore structure and surface chemistry control fluid storage, wettability and recovery in tight reservoir rocks, mainly diatomite and chalk. Her work uses laboratory characterization such as X-ray diffraction, mercury intrusion capillary pressure, surface area measurements, spontaneous imbibition tests and calcite precipitation experiments. The applications are enhanced oil recovery and subsurface CO2 storage, including comparisons of reservoir rocks with outcrop analogues from Norway, Greece and California.

name: Wiktor Waldemar Weibull
summary: Wiktor Waldemar Weibull works on seismic inversion and modelling, developing nonlinear amplitude-versus-offset methods that use adjoint-state gradients and quasi-Newton optimization to estimate elastic properties, attenuation, and time-lapse saturation and pressure changes. He tests these methods on synthetic and North Sea field data, compares them with deep learning approaches, and also works on seismic imaging, velocity analysis and full waveform inversion. His applied work includes reservoir and CO2 storage monitoring, salt and fault imaging, and shallow marine and near-surface surveys such as autonomous-vessel chirp sonar mapping of a buried shipwreck and 3D urban subsurface modelling.

name: Yasaman Cheraghi
summary: Yasaman Cheraghi studies sequential decision making under uncertainty in the energy sector, applying reinforcement learning, particle filtering, least squares Monte Carlo and statistical analysis. Her work includes automated geosteering systems for well placement that are benchmarked against human experts in a simulated competition environment, and analysis of decisions recorded from hundreds of geosteerers. She also develops decision frameworks for energy transition investment and compares learning-based and planning-based methods for real option valuation.

name: Zhixin Yu
summary: Zhixin Yu works on catalytic and electrochemical materials for energy and sustainability, including electrocatalysts for water splitting, photocatalytic hydrogen evolution, and supported catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol and biomass upgrading. Studies also cover protective interfaces and framework materials (COFs, HOFs, MOFs) for zinc and lithium metal battery anodes, as well as positron annihilation characterization of defects in biomimetic composites. Methods combine materials synthesis, electrochemical and catalytic testing, in situ spectroscopy and DFT calculations, with one review of CO2 capture technologies for bioenergy.

name: Åsmund Aamodt Resell
summary: Åsmund Aamodt Resell studies the mechanics of slender rods and pipes in curved and irregular boreholes, and the fluid flow in the annular gaps around them. The work combines beam theory and finite element modelling, for example for drill strings and casing with centralizers, with analytical solutions and computational fluid dynamics for flow and forces in eccentric annuli. The applications are well construction and drilling, with links to journal bearings and biomedical annular geometries.

name: Øystein Arild
summary: Øystein Arild's publications address well integrity in oil and gas wells, particularly how annulus cement sheaths are verified as barriers during permanent plugging and abandonment under the NORSOK D-010 standard. The work examines the 30 m cement length requirement and compares continuous with stacked bond log evidence, using flow and capillary pressure calculations alongside qualitative assessment of cracks and shear failure. A further strand covers data quality in drilling, with an analytical method to estimate bounds on the coefficient of determination so that gap-filling methods for real-time drilling logs can be assessed without ground truth.

name: Guizhou Wang
department: Faculty of Science and Technology (department not stated)
summary: Guizhou Wang studies cryptocurrencies, monetary systems and sustainable finance using game-theoretic models, differential-equation and stochastic simulation models, econometric estimation, and bibliometric reviews. The work covers competition between hard, fiat, digital and central bank currencies, Bitcoin price dynamics, interest rate determination, and the economics of Bitcoin mining in biorefineries. It also examines volatility spillovers among ESG-rated stocks in China and the development of green finance research, with implications for policymakers, financial institutions and investors.

name: Abhishek Banerjee
summary: Abhishek Banerjee studies TiFe alloys for solid-state hydrogen storage, focusing on how niobium doping changes crystal structure and hydrogen uptake. The work combines arc-melting synthesis, in situ synchrotron powder X-ray diffraction, EXAFS and hydrogen absorption measurements to link structure with activation and sorption kinetics. The findings are relevant to stationary hydrogen storage and the design of new storage materials.

name: Aksel Hiorth
summary: Aksel Hiorth works on modeling fluid flow and chemical processes in porous media and on computational hemodynamics. His publications use physics-informed neural networks, lattice Boltzmann simulation with multiple relaxation time operators, pore-scale image-based simulation, geochemical and reactive transport modeling (IORSim), and laboratory zeta potential and imbibition experiments. Applications include oil recovery and low-salinity waterflooding in carbonates, fractured reservoirs, field-scale reservoir simulation with CO2 footprint estimates, and cardiovascular problems such as wall shear stress, coronary flow reserve and venous assist pumps for Fontan patients.

name: Aleksi Kurkela
summary: Aleksi Kurkela works on the equation of state of dense matter in neutron stars, using Bayesian inference, Gaussian-process priors, and constraints from chiral effective field theory, perturbative QCD, gravitational-wave and X-ray observations to probe possible quark-matter cores. He also studies the early out-of-equilibrium stages of heavy-ion collisions with QCD kinetic theory, including jet quenching, heavy-quark diffusion, hydrodynamization attractors, a parton cascade code and neural-network evaluation of collision integrals. Related work covers transport properties such as the bulk viscosity of quark matter, using perturbative and holographic methods.

name: Alex Bentley Nielsen
summary: Alex Bentley Nielsen works on gravitational wave astronomy, using Bayesian parameter estimation on LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA data to test general relativity and to study black hole ringdown. His work includes searching for multiple ringdown modes and overtones in events such as GW190521 and GW150914, testing post-Newtonian phase corrections and the black hole area theorem, and constraining modified-gravity models including pseudo-complex GR and dirty black holes. He also develops waveform and analysis tools, such as line-of-sight acceleration corrections for compact binary signals and an effective-field-theory Lagrangian for the Kalb-Ramond field.

name: Alexander Rothkopf
summary: Alexander Rothkopf works on lattice quantum field theory and computational physics, covering heavy quark-antiquark potentials and quarkonium in the quark-gluon plasma, Casimir effects in non-Abelian gauge theory, and real-time simulations using complex Langevin methods with machine-learned kernels. He also develops variational discretization schemes based on summation-by-parts operators for initial value and boundary value problems, preserving symmetries and Noether charges and allowing automatic mesh refinement. Further work includes action principles for nonholonomic mechanics, non-Hermitian operators in quantum mechanics, and inverse-problem methods such as Bayesian spectral reconstruction.

name: Alexander Ulanovskii
summary: Alexander Ulanovskii works in harmonic and complex analysis, focusing on sampling and reconstruction in shift-invariant spaces, Paley-Wiener and Bernstein spaces, and Gabor frames generated by Gaussian, hyperbolic secant and related functions. His publications use function-theoretic and density-based methods to establish sharp sampling conditions, to study the geometry of unit balls (extreme and exposed points), and to analyse completeness of exponential systems and the stability of shifts and atomic measures. Application areas include signal reconstruction, mobile sampling along curves, and time-frequency analysis.

name: Anders Tranberg
summary: Anders Tranberg studies out-of-equilibrium quantum field theory, with a focus on real-time dynamics in the early Universe, including reheating after inflation, bubble nucleation, stochastic inflation and instabilities in SU(2) gauge theory. His methods include numerical lattice simulations of Kadanoff-Baym equations from 2PI effective action truncations, classical-statistical simulations, and Lefschetz thimble Monte Carlo techniques for real-time path integrals. He also applies these approaches to quantum corrections for solitonic objects such as Q-balls.

name: Bjørn Henrik Auestad
summary: Bjørn Henrik Auestad's publications span sports cardiology and psychiatry. In cardiology, studies of middle-aged recreational athletes use echocardiography, cardiac troponin measurements and coronary imaging to examine how prolonged high-intensity exercise affects heart function, myocardial efficiency and non-obstructive coronary disease. In psychiatry, work includes a randomized trial comparing electroconvulsive therapy with pharmacological treatment in bipolar depression using patient-reported outcomes, and a registry-linked longitudinal study of suicidality trajectories in first-episode psychosis analyzed with growth mixture modelling and regression.

name: Daniil Krichevskiy
summary: Daniil Krichevskiy works in theoretical particle physics, using effective field theory methods such as chiral perturbation theory to study strongly coupled gauge theories. His publications compute next-to-leading and next-to-next-to-leading order corrections for QCD-like theories with two fermion flavours, fit low-energy constants to lattice data for Sp(4) gauge theory, and apply the results to pion dark matter models such as SIMP. He has also studied the unitary Fermi gas in a harmonic trap in the large-charge and large-N limits, linking a microscopic theory to a superfluid effective description.

name: David Ploog
summary: David Ploog works in the representation theory of algebras and triangulated categories, focusing on simple-minded collections, simple-minded systems and bounded t-structures in cluster categories of acyclic quivers. His work uses categorical methods to establish bijections linking these objects to noncrossing partitions of Weyl groups. The results are theoretical and extend earlier results known for Dynkin quivers to the broader acyclic case.

name: Eirik Eik Svanes
summary: Eirik Eik Svanes studies the mathematical structure of heterotic string compactifications, focusing on moduli spaces of supersymmetric vacua on Calabi-Yau, SU(3) and G2 geometries. The work uses differential and complex geometry, cohomological and deformation-theory methods, and one-loop computations in holomorphic and topological field theories, including anomaly cancellation. Further publications cover moduli space metrics, string-inspired gravity corrections to binary dynamics, and discrete symmetries of five-dimensional superconformal theories.

name: Enrico Riccardi
summary: Enrico Riccardi develops computational methods for rare-event molecular simulation, including path sampling software and its use to study how drugs unbind from protein targets such as the ABL kinase. He also applies machine learning to other areas, including sparse multiple instance learning for immune receptor data, automated analysis of fish liver histology images for environmental monitoring, and reinforcement learning to manage CO2 injection rates in geological storage.

name: Eva Rauls
summary: Eva Rauls studies how macrocyclic supramolecular materials, especially pillar[n]arenes and dyn[4]arenes, capture and separate CO2 and other polluting gases. Her work combines density functional theory and tight-binding calculations with experimental synthesis, recrystallization, spectroscopy and gas adsorption measurements under dry and humid conditions. She has also used radio frequency scanning tunneling microscopy to probe dielectric relaxation in a single-molecule junction.

name: Germano Nardini
summary: Germano Nardini works on gravitational waves from the early universe and from compact binaries, with a focus on forecasting what the LISA space detector and other future observatories can measure. His publications use template-based signal reconstruction pipelines, Bayesian parameter inference, population modelling and Gaussian-process acceleration of inference, and also include theoretical work on phase transitions in warped extra-dimension models. Applications include inflation, cosmic strings, first-order phase transitions, primordial black holes, stellar-mass black-hole binaries and links to collider and pulsar timing array data.

name: Gøran Jan Nilsen
summary: Gøran Jan Nilsen works on neutron scattering studies of magnetic and molecular materials, combining inelastic and quasi-elastic scattering, diffraction, polarization analysis and density functional theory. His publications cover frustrated and low-dimensional quantum magnets such as breathing pyrochlore spinels, Kitaev candidates and spin chains, crystal-field levels in rare-earth permanent magnets, and Bayesian, simulation-informed analysis of molecular motion in liquid benzene. He also develops data-analysis methods, including a way to separate neutron cross-section components using a single polarization direction.

name: Helena Kolešová
summary: Helena Kolešová works on theoretical particle physics and cosmology, focusing on dark matter models and strongly coupled gauge theories. Her publications use chiral effective field theory with fits to lattice data, together with cosmic-ray upscattering calculations and sensitivity estimates for experiments such as DUNE and Xenon-1T. She also studies early-universe topics, including reheating through dark-sector confinement and gravitational waves from post-inflationary phase transitions, and the chiral soliton lattice in QCD at finite density and magnetic field.

name: Helge Paul Ruddat
summary: Helge Paul Ruddat works on mirror symmetry and enumerative geometry, focusing on log Calabi-Yau surfaces and their mirror families. His publications use logarithmic Gromov-Witten theory, the Gross-Siebert intrinsic mirror construction, tropical and toric degeneration techniques, period integrals and the topological vertex to relate curve counts to periods of mirror curves. The work covers Takahashi's conjecture for rational curves in the projective plane relative to a cubic, and q-refined, higher-genus open-closed correspondences for local Calabi-Yau geometries.

name: Jan Terje Kvaløy
summary: Jan Terje Kvaløy is a biostatistician who works on medical research, applying regression and survival methods to registry and clinical cohort data. His publications cover nationwide surgical outcomes studies of liver and pancreatic resection, intensive care for acute pancreatitis, and a cumulative sum (CUSUM) approach to monitoring survival in cancer registries using relative survival models. He also contributes to studies of maternal and newborn care in Tanzania, long-COVID and fatigue biomarkers, dry eye disease, and ctDNA detection with machine learning.

name: Jimmy Huy Tran
summary: Jimmy Huy Tran works on statistical methods for monitoring survival outcomes in health registries, developing cumulative sum (CUSUM) charts built on relative survival and excess hazard models to detect changes in survival time distributions while accounting for risk factors and uncertain cause of death. He also works on computational statistics, comparing adaptive tuning approaches for diagonal scale matrices in Hamiltonian Monte Carlo using numerical studies of sampling efficiency. Application areas include cancer registry surveillance and Bayesian sampling methodology.

name: Jörn Schulz
summary: Jörn Schulz works on statistical shape analysis, developing geometric representations such as skeletal models and elliptical tube models that keep objects valid and support mean shapes, hypothesis testing and analysis of joint variation across multiple objects. These methods are applied to brain structures such as the hippocampus and caudate in Parkinson's disease and autism. He also conducts clinical and epidemiological studies using regression and survival models on how orthostatic hypotension and sleep patterns relate to cognitive decline and dementia.

name: Konstantinos Alektoridis
summary: Konstantinos Alektoridis studies carbon dioxide capture using computational chemistry. His publication uses density-functional tight-binding (DFTB) calculations to compare how two functionalized dyn[4]arene macrocycles adsorb CO2, including binding inside the cavity and the uptake of multiple molecules until saturation. The work applies to materials for greenhouse gas capture and climate mitigation.

name: Martin Gunnar Gulbrandsen
summary: Martin Gunnar Gulbrandsen works in algebraic geometry, studying moduli spaces of geometric objects through Bridgeland stability conditions. His publication examines how the moduli space changes across walls, starting from the Hilbert scheme of pairs of skew lines in projective 3-space, and uses Mori theory to show the resulting spaces are smooth and projective. The work is theoretical and concerns the birational geometry of Hilbert schemes and related moduli spaces.

name: Olena Zavorotynska
summary: Olena Zavorotynska studies functional inorganic materials, including hydrogen storage alloys and hydrides (TiFe, magnesium borohydride) and zirconium and cerium metal-organic frameworks. Her work relies on synchrotron X-ray diffraction, X-ray absorption, Raman and infrared spectroscopy, often applied in situ to follow how materials form, transform or decompose. Application areas covered include solid-state hydrogen storage, CO2 and other gas adsorption, silver recovery from solution, and energy-efficient mechanochemical synthesis of oxides.

name: Quoc Duy Ho
summary: Quoc Duy Ho studies materials at the atomic scale, mainly through density functional theory, hybrid functional and molecular dynamics calculations, with machine-learning force fields used in some work on thermal transport. The research covers gas adsorption and CO2 capture in pillar[n]arene supramolecular frameworks, including some experimental adsorption and spectroscopy work. It also covers the electronic and magnetic properties of doped graphene and germanene nanoribbons, defects and dopants in β-Ga2O3, and thermal transport and phase transitions in 2D carbon and silicon materials, with applications in carbon capture, electronics, optoelectronics and spintronics.

name: Sigbjørn Hervik
summary: Sigbjørn Hervik works in pseudo-Riemannian geometry, studying left-invariant metrics on Lie groups and the structure of Lie algebras through group actions and the moving bracket approach. His work also covers the construction of new Einstein spaces by deforming symmetric ones, using scalar polynomial curvature invariants and (para-)Kähler structures. The research is mathematical and theoretical, with results in classification and explicit examples across different metric signatures.

name: Tomas Brauner
summary: Tomas Brauner works in theoretical physics on effective field theories, spontaneous symmetry breaking and scattering amplitudes. His publications use field-theoretic and geometric methods, including soft bootstrap and recursion techniques, to study amplitude structure, dualities between theories, Nambu-Goldstone bosons and dipole symmetries, and also nonrelativistic systems. He also applies chiral effective theory to dense QCD matter in magnetic fields, mapping phases such as chiral soliton lattices and vortex lattices, and has written a book and teaching article on related topics.

name: Tore Selland Kleppe
summary: Tore Selland Kleppe develops Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms for Bayesian computation, focusing on Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, the No-U-Turn Sampler, step-size and scale tuning, Riemann manifold metrics, randomized numerical integrators and sampling on constrained domains. Methods are tested on multiscale and high-dimensional distributions and on hierarchical models, with supporting theory and software. He also applies Bayesian state-space and stochastic volatility models and economic modelling to commodity and oil markets, covering futures curves, volatility regimes and storage.

name: Tyson Ritter
summary: Tyson Ritter works in several complex variables, studying proper holomorphic embeddings of multiply connected domains into the complex plane. The publication builds parametric versions of the Andersén–Lempert procedure and Carleman-type approximation so that whole continuous families of domains can be embedded at once. The work is theoretical and rooted in complex analysis and approximation theory.

name: Adugna Deressa Akessa
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Adugna Deressa Akessa studies additive manufacturing of polymers, fiber-reinforced composites and metals, linking process parameters to mechanical behavior and microstructure. The work combines mechanical testing, fracture and microstructure analysis, heat treatment, numerical simulation and Gaussian Process Regression machine learning to predict and optimize properties of printed parts. Materials examined include PLA+, carbon fiber with Onyx, Inconel 625 made by wire arc additive manufacturing, and 17-4 PH stainless steel.

name: Anders Sagvåg Birkemo
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science

name: Ayushi Rai
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Ayushi Rai studies thermochromic vanadium dioxide (VO2) thin films, including VO2/TiO2 bilayers, grown by pulsed laser deposition on substrates such as quartz, glass, silicon and LSAT. Her work links nanoscale structure, strain, grain morphology and phase composition to the metal–insulator transition and to electrical and optical switching, using transmission electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction, tip-enhanced and confocal Raman spectroscopy, and electrical measurements. The application focus is energy-efficient smart window coatings.

name: Bjørn Helge Hjertager
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science

name: Bjørn Skaare
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Bjørn Skaare studies marine operations for offshore wind turbines, focusing on decommissioning of bottom-fixed foundations and on maintenance access to floating turbines. The work uses time-domain simulation, finite element soil modelling and frequency-domain hydrodynamic analysis to examine crane barge response during monopile extraction and the motion of spar and semi-submersible platforms. It also includes a review of existing foundation removal methods, with application to offshore wind planning and operations.

name: Bruno Villoria
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Bruno Villoria studies fatigue of welded details in long-span suspension bridges, focusing on orthotropic steel and aluminium bridge decks under multiaxial, non-proportional and variable-amplitude loading. The work develops and compares assessment methods, including grain scale plasticity-based models, equivalent structural stress and strain approaches with path-dependent cycle counting, and new damage accumulation rules, validated against published fatigue tests. It also applies finite element analysis and time-domain simulation of stochastic traffic and wind loading to case-study bridges to estimate the fatigue life of critical joints.

name: Chern Fong Lee
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Chern Fong Lee studies floating offshore wind turbines, especially combined wind and wave energy systems that pair semi-submersible platforms with wave energy converters, as well as multi-rotor and shared-mooring configurations. The work relies on fully coupled time-domain simulation, analytical design methods and statistical extreme-response techniques to assess platform motions, power performance, and mooring line tensions and snap loads, with emphasis on intermediate water depths and synthetic fibre ropes. Related studies cover dynamic power cable models, vibration-based mooring damage detection, floating vertical axis turbines, turbine upscaling and subsea pipelaying simulation.

name: Dileepa Chathuranga Hettiarachchi
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Dileepa Chathuranga Hettiarachchi studies low-carbon cement binders, mortars and concrete in which large shares of Portland cement are replaced by silicomanganese slag, Icelandic volcanic pozzolan and ground granulated blast furnace slag. The work combines laboratory testing of strength, shrinkage, workability and heat of hydration with microstructural and mineralogical analysis (SEM, XRD, FTIR, TGA, calorimetry), and also uses response surface methodology to build predictive mix-design models. The application area is reducing clinker use and CO2 emissions in construction while keeping mechanical performance.

name: Dimitrios Pavlou
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Dimitrios Pavlou studies the fatigue, fracture and structural integrity of steel structures, covering multiaxial fatigue damage models, machine learning life prediction, stress concentration factors in welded tubular joints, and buckling of beams with web openings or corrosion. His work also includes hydrogen embrittlement and corrosion of pipeline steels, tested through mechanical testing, fractography and statistical analysis of incident data. He further applies analytical, finite element and computational fluid dynamics methods to offshore structures, including wind turbine dynamics, living breakwaters and aquaculture systems, and reviews structural health monitoring for marine structures.

name: Endalkachew Mosisa Gutema
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Endalkachew Mosisa Gutema studies advanced and sustainable materials and manufacturing, including natural fiber composites made from enset fiber, aluminum alloy composites reinforced with carbon nanotubes, and the machining of metal matrix composites. His methods include stir casting, powder metallurgy, stereolithography 3D printing, mechanical and microstructural testing, and statistical and genetic-algorithm optimization (RSM, ANOVA, MOGA). He has also applied structural equation modeling to examine how additive manufacturing practices affect supply chain performance in Ethiopian footwear industries.

name: Espen Undheim
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Espen Undheim works on laser-based directed energy deposition, a metal additive manufacturing process, applied to super duplex stainless steel. The publication uses Taguchi-designed experiments and weighted grey relational analysis to optimise process settings such as laser power, deposition speed, pulse frequency and shielding gas flow. Builds are assessed through density measurement, tensile testing, electron microscopy and diffraction to link process parameters with melt pool shape, porosity, microstructure and ductility.

name: Even Englund
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Even Englund studies the fatigue behaviour and structural integrity of girth-welded S355 steel tubular structures, with a focus on welds and repair welds placed in close proximity. The work combines laboratory fatigue testing, S-N curve development, hot-spot stress analysis, residual stress measurement (sectioning with strain gauges, X-ray diffraction), digital image correlation and finite element modelling with continuum damage. Application areas include offshore structures, pipelines, risers, wind turbine towers and tubular trusses, where the results inform design standards and test specimen selection.

name: Gerhard Ersdal
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Gerhard Ersdal works on the assessment of existing structures, using structural reliability, probabilistic and risk analysis to handle uncertainty in engineering decisions. His 2024 paper reviews risk-informed decision-making methods, discusses their limitations when applied to ageing structures, and proposes ideas to address them. The work considers how information from inspections, observed loading and material testing can be incorporated into assessments.

name: Guang Yin
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Guang Yin works on computational modelling of fluid flow and structural response for offshore and marine engineering. The publications use CFD (largely OpenFOAM and SedFoam solvers), reduced-order and theoretical models, and machine-learning approaches such as neural networks and physics-informed neural networks, and apply them to fish cages and aquaculture vessel tanks, subsea pipeline scour and vibration, umbilical cables, trimaran resistance and floating wind turbine moorings. Much of the work targets design-stage tools, including dissolved oxygen and hypoxia assessment in aquaculture, hydrodynamic load prediction near the seabed, and surrogate-based mooring optimization.

name: Hadi Pezeshki
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Hadi Pezeshki works on the fatigue and structural dynamics of engineering structures, with two main strands. One develops stress analysis methods, experiments and damage models to predict fatigue life under proportional and nonproportional multiaxial loading. The other develops analytical and numerical models of offshore monopile wind turbines, covering wave loading, soil-structure interaction, natural frequencies and gyroscopic effects, and he has also reviewed structural health monitoring methods for offshore and marine structures.

name: Hirpa Gelgele Lemu
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Hirpa Gelgele Lemu works on additive manufacturing and materials engineering, covering wire arc additive manufacturing of Inconel 718, 3D printing of polymer and natural-fiber composites (enset, sisal, cellulose, microalgae starch), and 4D printing of PLA. His methods combine experiments (microscopy, X-ray diffraction, thermal analysis, mechanical and rheological testing) with finite element, Monte Carlo and thermodynamic modeling. Application areas include bone tissue scaffolds based on triply periodic minimal surfaces, energy-absorbing honeycomb and foam structures, boiler tube thermo-structural analysis, and aluminum nanocomposites.

name: Idriss El-Thalji
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Idriss El-Thalji works on maintenance engineering and asset management, with a focus on predictive maintenance of wind turbines using vibration data, machine learning and deep learning for fault detection and remaining useful life forecasting. He also builds agent-based and other simulation models to study system availability, spare parts supply, offshore logistics and hospital emergency department patient flow. Further work covers risk-based maintenance practice in offshore industry, Industry 4.0 readiness, and engineering education methods such as gamified flipped classrooms.

name: Jakob Emanuel Beer
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science

name: Jan Frick
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Jan Frick studies logistics and supply chain management, with a focus on resilience, customs compliance, and digital information flows in cross-border trade. The work combines conceptual framework and reference-architecture design, scenario and sensitivity analysis, literature reviews, expert interviews and an empirical warehouse case study. Application areas include maritime chokepoint disruption, AI-supported document handling, EU product passports and carbon border rules, 3PL warehouse storage, collaborative freight exchanges, and blockchain in the energy sector.

name: Jan Magne Nygård
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science

name: Jan-Tore Jakobsen
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science

name: Jarle Berge
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Jarle Berge studies the structural behavior of aluminum columns, focusing on global buckling of extruded rectangular hollow profiles made from the 6082-T6 alloy. The work combines laboratory compression and cyclic loading tests, with digital image correlation to track deflection and strain, and compares the results with Eurocode 9 and Euler buckling calculations. It applies to structural design and code assessment for aluminum construction, including the safety margins in current design rules.

name: Jasna Bogunovic Jakobsen
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Jasna Bogunovic Jakobsen studies wind effects on long-span bridges, buildings and offshore structures, using wind tunnel tests, full-scale field monitoring with sonic anemometers, lidars and pressure sensors, and numerical simulation including large eddy simulation. Related work covers fatigue of welded steel and aluminum bridge details under combined wind and traffic loading, atmospheric boundary layer wind profiles and turbulence for floating wind turbines, and ship and barge collisions with bridges. Application domains include bridge design, structural health monitoring, urban pedestrian wind comfort and wind energy.

name: Jawad Raza
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science

name: Jayantha Prasanna Liyanage
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Jayantha Prasanna Liyanage studies how operators of complex, high-risk industrial systems can detect and make sense of process deviations early, using concepts such as advanced situation awareness, contextual knowledge and hybrid decision-support solutions. The work draws on conceptual analysis, review of industrial cases and collaboration with industry, with applications in remote operations, rotating machinery in oil refineries and digitalized industrial assets. It also covers asset management, including industrial agility as a strategic capability for asset-centric organizations in industrial eco-systems.

name: Jianan Zhang
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Jianan Zhang develops numerical models of floating dock operations, representing the dock and docked vessel as six-degree-of-freedom rigid bodies under hydrostatic, hydrodynamic, mooring and contact loads, with hydraulic models of ballast water systems. The work covers automatic ballast control with a modified P-controller, stability and structural bending analysis, and simulation of failure cases such as valve or pump faults and corroded ballast tanks. Model-scale and full-scale tests are used to validate the models, and earlier work includes finite element simulation of ice floe sliding impact on ship hull structures.

name: Jon Erik Karlsen
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Jon Erik Karlsen studies how metal additive manufacturing and rapid casting can supply on-demand replacements for obsolete or undocumented components on ageing offshore installations on the Norwegian Continental Shelf. His work combines literature review, a roadmap and flow chart for the on-demand supply chain, and a multi-criteria decision analysis (Analytic Hierarchy Process) with industry expert input, applied to a valve body case from Statfjord-A. The outputs are intended for energy, oil and gas asset owners, suppliers and engineers.

name: Jonas Thor Snæbjörnsson
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Jonas Thor Snæbjörnsson studies wind effects on long-span bridges and other slender structures, combining full-scale field monitoring (surface pressure systems, sonic anemometers, vibration sensors) with wind tunnel tests and numerical modelling. The work covers bridge buffeting theory for skew and inhomogeneous winds, turbulence simulation, system identification of bridge and cable dynamics, and lidar-based wind measurements in wind tunnels, urban sites and offshore settings. Applications include cable-stayed, suspension and floating bridge design, as well as offshore wind energy and coastal wind assessment using satellite data and CFD.

name: Kenneth Alasdair Macdonald
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science

name: Kjell Tore Fosså
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Kjell Tore Fosså studies low-carbon cement-based materials, focusing on replacing large shares of cement with silicomanganese slag, Icelandic volcanic pozzolan and blast furnace slag. The work uses compressive strength tests, calorimetry, SEM and XRD, shrinkage measurements, and response surface modelling to link hydration, microstructure and mechanical performance in pastes, mortars and high-strength concrete. He has also carried out large-scale experiments and nonlinear finite element simulations of crack spacing in reinforced concrete members.

name: Knut Erik Teigen Giljarhus
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Knut Erik Teigen Giljarhus works on computational fluid dynamics and its combination with machine learning, with applications in urban wind and pedestrian comfort, sports aerodynamics, and non-Newtonian and annular flows relevant to drilling and bearings. His publications compare RANS and large eddy simulation against wind tunnel data, propose validation metrics, and build deep learning surrogate models (such as MLP-Mixer networks) that predict wind or drag far faster than full simulations. He also applies data-driven methods to wind energy, covering unsupervised fault detection in turbine blades, remaining useful life forecasting for bearings, and optimization of floating turbine power cables.

name: Lennart Vogt
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Lennart Vogt studies atmospheric wind and turbulence for wind energy, using lidar, sonic and cup anemometer measurements from coastal, offshore North Sea and urban sites. His work compares analytical wind profile models for stable atmospheric conditions with observations, fits empirical turbulence spectra and coherence models, and uses simulations to test how stability-dependent wind profiles affect the motions of a 15-MW floating wind turbine.

name: Lichao Xiong
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Lichao Xiong studies floating offshore wind systems that combine multiple rotors with wave energy converters on a shared semi-submersible platform. The work uses an in-house, fully coupled time-domain simulation tool built on OpenModelica, checked against commercial software, to analyse platform motion, yaw control with a linear quadratic regulator, and mooring loads. Applications include comparing deep and intermediate water sites and assessing how torus-type converters affect power capture and platform motion.

name: Lin Li
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Lin Li studies the dynamics, design and reliability of floating offshore structures, including floating wind turbines, offshore fish farm cages and multi-body marine systems. The work combines time-domain hydrodynamic and mooring simulation, Kriging surrogate models, sensitivity and reliability analysis, and faster ODE solving schemes with analysis of metocean and wind data (hindcast and lidar). Applications include shared mooring design, aquaculture-wind co-location, installation operations such as jacket lift-off, and site conditions for floating wind arrays.

name: Lorents Reinås
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science

name: M. K. Samarakoon
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: M. K. Samarakoon studies low-carbon cementitious materials, focusing on mortars in which large shares of Portland cement are replaced by Icelandic volcanic pozzolan and silicon manganese slag, an industrial byproduct. The work uses compressive strength testing over 3 to 56 days, scanning electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction and isothermal calorimetry to assess strength, microstructure and heat development. The application area is sustainable construction, aiming to cut clinker use and CO2 emissions where fly ash is becoming less available.

name: Madushan Madhava Jayalath
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Madushan Madhava Jayalath studies agri-food and vegetable supply chains in developing economies, with a focus on Sri Lanka, covering waste, price volatility, disruption risk, rural finance and food security. The work combines fuzzy inference systems, risk registers, analytic hierarchy process, interpretive structural modelling, Delphi studies, time series analysis, social network analysis, value chain analysis and process modelling, often through case studies and stakeholder input. Applications include digitalization and digital transformation, circular economy practices, risk assessment and policy recommendations for smallholder farmers and supply chain actors.

name: Makafui Kwame Botsoe
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Makafui Kwame Botsoe studies reliability, availability and predictive maintenance of engineered assets. The publications compare deep learning and statistical time-series forecasting methods, including an LSTM autoencoder paired with Prophet, ARIMA and GRU, for predicting the remaining useful life of wind turbine bearings from vibration data. They also use agent-based simulation to compare availability estimates for subsea safety equipment at equipment and component levels.

name: Mesay Tolcha
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Mesay Tolcha works on materials and manufacturing engineering, covering the degradation of silicon solar cells, the machining of metal matrix composites, and the mechanical behavior of metals. Methods include field measurements and systematic literature review for photovoltaics, analytical modeling, finite element simulation, deep neural networks and multi-criteria optimization for machining and metal processing, and rheological testing of microalgae starch for 3D-printable bioplastics. Application areas include solar energy in hot-humid climates, energy-efficient and cost-effective machining, continuous casting, and sustainable additive manufacturing.

name: Minh Jimmy Le
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Minh Jimmy Le studies the hydrodynamic resistance of trimaran vessels, focusing on how outrigger layout and forward speed affect the form factor used to estimate total resistance. The work combines OpenFOAM computational fluid dynamics simulations validated against experiments with potential flow theory for wave-making resistance, and more recently a neural network trained on the simulation results to predict the form factor. The applications are early-stage ship design and optimization of outrigger arrangements.

name: Mona Wetrhus Minde
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Mona Wetrhus Minde studies how materials change at the microscale, covering both fine-grained carbonate reservoir rocks and metal alloys. Her work on North Sea chalk uses brine flooding experiments with electron, helium ion and X-ray methods to track mineral dissolution, precipitation, fracture change and rock weakening, and she has also characterised aged well cement. She has additionally examined the microstructure, crystallographic texture and mechanical behaviour of super duplex stainless steel made by directed laser deposition.

name: Morten Andre Langøy
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Morten Andre Langøy studies how safety and environmental risk is regulated and governed in the offshore oil and gas industry, with a focus on Norway and comparisons with the US. His work develops conceptual models that compare functional and prescriptive regulatory regimes, drawing on legal traditions, trust between industry and regulator, and case material such as a national audit of the Norwegian petroleum safety authority. The models are intended to help assess regulatory effectiveness and may be applied in other hazardous industries.

name: Muk Chen Ong
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Muk Chen Ong's publications cover marine and offshore engineering, including floating offshore wind turbines (optimization, mooring and power cable dynamics), offshore aquaculture (fish cages and shipboard tanks), ocean current energy devices, and ship hydrodynamics and stability. The work relies on computational fluid dynamics, time-domain coupled simulation, reduced-order and quasi-static models, and machine learning approaches such as neural networks and physics-informed networks. Application areas include offshore wind design, aquaculture oxygen management and structural monitoring, marine operations, and vessel and floating dock design.

name: Navid Sayyar
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Navid Sayyar studies laser-based directed energy deposition of super duplex stainless steel, examining how process parameters, pulsed versus continuous laser input and post-deposition annealing shape microstructure, crystallographic texture, mechanical properties and corrosion behaviour. The work combines designed experiments (Taguchi, grey relational analysis) with electron microscopy, EBSD, tensile and impact testing, and electrochemical measurements. Related publications cover cold rolling and precipitation hardening of Inconel 718 and thermal management of thermoelectric modules using phase change material and metal foam.

name: Nirosha D. Adasooriya
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Nirosha D. Adasooriya studies the structural integrity and durability of pipelines, offshore wind turbine structures and concrete buildings. The work combines laboratory mechanical testing, fractography and microstructure analysis of pipeline steel exposed to hydrogen, statistical analysis of corrosion incident records, conceptual assessment frameworks and fatigue curves. Application areas include hydrogen and natural gas transport, offshore renewable energy, and sustainable, prefabricated and reusable construction methods.

name: Noorhan Firdaus Pambudi
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Noorhan Firdaus Pambudi studies circular economy business models and plastic and household waste management in Indonesia. The work combines large-scale community surveys with statistical modelling (regression, cluster analysis), risk and factor prioritisation methods (FMEA, DEMATEL, causal-loop diagrams), system dynamics simulation, scenario planning, and case studies of waste management start-ups using social media data. Applications cover public participation in waste segregation and recycling, waste worker conditions, collaboration between start-ups, government and industry, and policy and business strategy for a green transition.

name: Nursultan Jyeniskhan
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Nursultan Jyeniskhan works on digital twins and cyber-physical systems for additive manufacturing, with a focus on fused deposition modeling 3D printers. The publication builds a digital twin that combines convolutional neural network anomaly detection with model predictive control of material feed, and proposes real-time frameworks to guard against cyber-attacks. The work applies to smart manufacturing plants that need safer and more reliable process control.

name: Ove Kjetil Mikkelsen
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science

name: Ove Tobias Gudmestad
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Ove Tobias Gudmestad's publications address offshore and marine engineering, covering structural loading and dynamic impact, support structures and power cables for offshore wind, and the safety of subsea cables and pipelines. His work also covers metocean conditions such as extreme waves in the Baltic and polar lows in the Barents Sea, Arctic shipping risk and environmental impact analysis, and climate-adapted design. Further papers deal with maritime education and simulator-based training, ship damage stability, offshore resource use in Vietnam, fish farming, and liquid hydrogen valve design, using literature reviews, case studies, statistical hindcast analysis and qualitative risk methods.

name: R. M. Chandima Ratnayake
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: R. M. Chandima Ratnayake studies the fatigue behaviour of welded tubular structures, using laboratory cyclic tensile testing of S355 girth weld specimens to develop S–N curves, stress concentration factors and design guidance for closely spaced welds. The work also covers supply chain and business model research, where multi-case benchmarking with the Business Model Canvas and secondary data analysis are used to examine digital product passports, EU packaging regulation and market access for Sri Lankan tea smallholders. Application areas include trusses, risers and pipelines, as well as sustainable and circular agri-food systems.

name: R. M.Chandima Ratnayake
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: R. M. Chandima Ratnayake's work spans risk and reliability engineering, fatigue of welded steel structures, and sustainable supply chains. The publications use fuzzy inference systems, Bayesian networks, analytic hierarchy process, causal loop diagrams and survey statistics to assess risks and policies in smallholder agri-food and healthcare supply chains, alongside experimental fatigue testing, digital image correlation and finite element modelling of closely spaced S355 girth welds. Related studies address asset integrity management, digital twins and AI-enabled decision support for power distribution and oil and gas, and digital value stream mapping in engineering-to-order projects.

name: S. M.Samindi M.K. Samarakoon
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: S. M. Samindi M.K. Samarakoon's research covers low-carbon construction materials, circular economy and waste management, and sustainable performance in buildings and engineering organisations. Laboratory work tests cement binders, mortars and concretes that replace cement with industrial by-products, volcanic pozzolan or treated textile waste, using strength testing, calorimetry, SEM/XRD analysis and response surface modelling. Other studies use surveys, interviews, scenario planning, risk and decision-analysis methods, simulation, life cycle costing and case studies to examine plastic waste management in Indonesia, building energy and water efficiency, and digital process and performance management in engineering-to-order firms.

name: S. Roemer
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: S. Roemer studies wind flow in urban settings using remote sensing, in particular continuous-wave nacelle lidars and a vertical wind profiler deployed on a university campus. The work compares lidar-derived horizontal wind speeds with sonic anemometer data, fits logarithmic and power-law profiles to estimate wind shear and surface roughness, and analyses turbulence spectra and variances. The measurements are intended for wind monitoring around buildings and for validating numerical models of urban flow.

name: Samdar Kakay
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Samdar Kakay studies the lateral-torsional buckling of steel I-beams using laboratory three-point bending tests on several cross sections and beam lengths. The work measures load and lateral displacement of the compression flange to derive buckling moment capacities and elastic critical moments, then checks them against Eurocode 3 design methods. The research applies to structural steel design and verification of beam stability.

name: Shangming Wang
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Shangming Wang studies ship hydrodynamics, focusing on resistance prediction for trimarans with different outrigger layouts and forward speeds. The work combines CFD simulations in OpenFOAM, potential flow theory and neural networks to derive and predict form factors, and also develops a harmonic polynomial cell method with overlapping grids for floating-body radiation problems. Applications include early-stage vessel design, hull form optimization and seakeeping analysis.

name: Soheil Salahshour
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
