summary: Soheil Salahshour studies the decommissioning of offshore wind turbine foundations, focusing on removing monopiles from the seabed by vibratory extraction and hydraulic pressure. The work uses finite element modelling (Coupled Eulerian-Lagrangian analysis in ABAQUS with modified soil models) for sand and clay, and time-domain simulations and extreme value analysis of crane barge motion, wire tension and allowable sea states. He has also reviewed decommissioning methods and has combined experiments with finite element analysis of stress in mechanical pin joints.

name: Sudath C. Siriwardane
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Sudath C. Siriwardane's research centres on the fatigue, durability and structural integrity of steel, aluminium, concrete and timber structures. The publications cover multiaxial and variable-amplitude fatigue models, orthotropic bridge decks, wind turbines, flare booms, pipelines, corroded reinforced concrete, buckling of beams and timber-concrete slabs, using analytical derivation, finite element and numerical simulation, statistical analysis and laboratory testing. Application areas include bridges, offshore and onshore wind energy, oil and gas infrastructure and nature-based coastal protection structures.

name: Tor Henning Hemmingsen
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Tor Henning Hemmingsen studies corrosion in energy infrastructure, using electrochemical experiments to examine how weak acids such as carbonic, acetic and formic acid drive carbon steel corrosion in petroleum pipelines. His work also covers environment-assisted damage in offshore wind turbine structures, with a conceptual assessment framework and a new fatigue curve for welded tubular joints validated against experimental fatigue lives. In addition, he has contributed to computational modelling and depth control of a subsea shuttle tanker concept for liquid CO2 transport.

name: Udo Zimmermann
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Udo Zimmermann studies how mineral composition and texture control the behavior of rocks in subsurface energy applications and in the geological record. His work combines laboratory mechanical and flow tests, electron and helium ion microscopy, XRD, geochemistry and detrital zircon dating to examine salt caverns for hydrogen storage, chalk and tight gas reservoirs, and CO2 storage. He also applies sedimentary petrography, geochemistry and provenance analysis to Paleozoic basins of the central Andes.

name: Usman Shaukat
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Usman Shaukat studies urban wind environments at pedestrian level using computational fluid dynamics, comparing large eddy simulation (LES) with Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) models against wind tunnel measurements on benchmark cases such as the Michelstadt array and the Niigata district. His work develops validation metrics for LES, provides turbulent inflow datasets, and applies statistical distribution models to gusts and low wind speed events. The application areas are pedestrian wind comfort assessment and urban planning.

name: Vidar Folke Hansen
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Vidar Folke Hansen studies how processing shapes the microstructure and properties of metals and functional thin films. His work covers laser-based additive manufacturing of super duplex stainless steel, Inconel 718 and 316L steel, using parameter optimization, heat treatment, mechanical testing and electron microscopy with texture analysis. He also characterizes thermochromic VO2 thin films for smart windows, along with thermoelectric materials and magnesium corrosion, using TEM, Raman spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction.

name: W. Madushan Fernando
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: W. Madushan Fernando studies smallholder agri-food supply chains in developing economies, with Sri Lankan tea producers as the main case. The work uses decision-support and systems methods such as analytic hierarchy process, TOPSIS, causal loop diagrams, interpretive structural modeling, fuzzy inference and cluster analysis, alongside case studies and surveys. Topics include supply chain inefficiencies and waste, policy analysis and risk assessment, digital and mobile technology adoption, voluntary sustainability standards, and SME digital maturity.

name: Wakshum Mekonnen Tucho
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Wakshum Mekonnen Tucho studies metal and polymer additive manufacturing, including laser directed energy deposition, laser powder bed fusion, wire arc and filament-based printing. This work links process parameters and heat treatment to microstructure, porosity, hardness, tensile strength and toughness in alloys such as super duplex stainless steel, Inconel 625 and 718, AlSi10Mg and 316L, using Taguchi and grey relational optimization, electron microscopy and machine learning prediction. He also works on materials for CO2 conversion and capture, covering MOF-supported Cu/ZnO methanol synthesis catalysts, sulfonic acid Zr-MOFs, dual-atom electrocatalysts, plus mechanochemical synthesis and cellulose nanocrystals.

name: Waqar Ali
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Waqar Ali works on predictive maintenance and condition monitoring of wind turbines, focusing on blade faults such as cracks and erosion and on bearing degradation. His work applies vibration signal analysis, feature engineering, machine learning and deep learning, including autoencoders, anomaly detectors and time-series forecasting models for remaining useful life prediction. He also reviews erosion monitoring methods and proposes risk-based frameworks for evaluating prognostic models in maintenance decisions.

name: Xueliang Wen
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Xueliang Wen studies marine and offshore engineering problems using numerical modelling, including CFD, rigid-body dynamics and surrogate-based optimization, with some experimental validation. The work covers offshore fish farming (cage structural response, net and tendon damage detection, dissolved oxygen and hypoxia risk), floating docks, suspension ships, floating wind and solar platforms and mooring design, and scour and vibration of subsea pipelines. Applications include aquaculture design, ship and dock operational safety, renewable energy structures and seabed infrastructure.

name: Yanyan Sha
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Yanyan Sha studies how marine and civil structures respond to extreme loads, especially ship and barge collisions with floating bridges, bridge piers and offshore wind turbine floaters. Her work combines nonlinear finite element simulation (LS-DYNA, OrcaFlex), probabilistic risk analysis using ship traffic data, and wind-induced response modelling for floating bridges. She also investigates rock fracturing in blasting under in-situ stress, using laboratory model tests with digital image correlation together with theoretical and numerical analysis, and examines impact behaviour of concrete materials such as UHPC, prestressed and fibre-reinforced concrete.

name: Yihan Xing
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Yihan Xing works on the dynamics, loads and safety of offshore and marine structures, including floating offshore wind turbines and farms, wave energy converters, moored vessels and wharves, and autonomous underwater vehicles. Methods include coupled time-domain simulation (e.g. OpenFAST, ANSYS-AQWA), active learning Kriging surrogates for fatigue and power assessment, deep learning time-series models such as TimesNet, and risk methods such as Bayesian networks, alongside laboratory model tests of liquid dampers. Applications cover fatigue and extreme load estimation, wake steering and yaw control, mooring failure and tension prediction, thruster fault detection, and inland vessel manoeuvring.

name: Yosef W. Adugna
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Yosef W. Adugna works on additive manufacturing and its use in biomedical and engineering settings. His publications cover 3D-printed triply periodic minimal surface scaffolds for bone tissue engineering, tested for strength, energy absorption and cell attachment, as well as cellulose-reinforced PLA composites for 4D printing and residual stresses in wire arc additive manufacturing. He also applies reverse engineering, 3D scanning and finite element or meshless stress analysis to the femur and medical models, and uses analytical modeling, neural networks and response surface methods to optimize machining of aluminum composites.

name: Yu Ma
department: Mechanical and Structural Engineering and Materials Science
summary: Yu Ma studies the numerical modeling and design of floating offshore structures, especially steel-framed fish cages and floating wind turbines connected by shared mooring lines. The work uses time-domain simulation, catenary mooring formulations, MATLAB and SIMA codes, Kriging surrogate models with Sobol sensitivity analysis, and a relaxation scheme for adaptive-time-step ODE solvers that speeds up convolution calculations. Applications include offshore aquaculture, offshore wind co-location, mooring design and digital-twin simulation of marine dynamic systems.

name: Alexander Kuran
summary: Alexander Kuran studies how the education of customs officers in Norway has changed with the move from in-house training to an academic bachelor's degree in customs and border control. His work looks at organizational change, workplace culture, recruitment and the passing of tacit knowledge from experienced staff to new graduates. He uses an exploratory qualitative approach based on conversations with students, field observation and interviews with customs officials, and proposes a follow-up research agenda.

name: Alexander Trengereid
summary: Alexander Trengereid studies public sector crisis management, with a focus on how Norway's government handled the COVID-19 pandemic. His work examines risk reduction, decision-making structures, leadership, crisis communication and learning, mainly at the central government level but also touching on local authorities and the international level. It considers how governance capacity and legitimacy interact to support public cooperation and trust.

name: Ana Llopis Alvarez
summary: Ana Llopis Alvarez studies how people experience their homes and neighbourhoods in Norway, covering household energy behaviour and quality of life among local and immigrant residents. Her work uses questionnaire surveys, map-based interviews, and geographic and statistical analysis to link housing circumstances, neighbourhood conditions and smart energy app use to residents' satisfaction and daily practices. The findings are aimed at residential planning, housing design, app development and policy for sustainable household energy use.

name: Anders Riel Müller
summary: Anders Riel Müller studies urban development and the energy transition, with a focus on Stavanger, Norway, using qualitative case studies, ethnography, participatory workshops, discourse and media analysis, and topic modelling of social media data. His work examines smart city policy and narratives, inclusive and participatory planning (including children's participation), post-petroleum and net zero imaginaries, and frontier-making in Scandinavia. Other publications address leadership in Positive Energy Districts, and compare calculated and measured energy use in municipal buildings.

name: Andreea-Laura Cojocaru
summary: Andreea-Laura Cojocaru studies the economics and regulation of fisheries and aquaculture, with a focus on Norwegian salmon farming and whitefish fisheries. Her work uses econometric methods such as difference-in-differences and discrete choice models, along with fine-scale production data and global performance comparisons, to examine quotas, seasonality, landing decisions and policy instruments like feed-in tariffs. It also covers coastal communities, food security and the sustainable transformation of aquatic food systems.

name: Ari Krisna Mawira Tarigan
summary: Ari Krisna Mawira Tarigan studies urban sustainability, with a focus on green infrastructure, nature-based solutions, sustainable mobility, and household and corporate sustainability behaviour. The work draws on spatial indicator assessment, systematic reviews, surveys, interviews, structural equation and nested logit modelling, and text mining of social media and app reviews. Application areas include city planning in Stavanger, Jakarta, Gdańsk and Indonesian energy governance, children's outdoor learning, smart energy apps, and the circular economy.

name: Atle Øglend
summary: Atle Øglend studies the economics of seafood and commodity markets, with a focus on Norwegian salmon aquaculture, export supply chains and international trade. His work uses firm-level customs and production data, econometric methods such as cointegration analysis, instrumental variables and quasi-natural experiments, and theoretical models to examine intermediaries, foreign processing, agglomeration, trade shocks (Brexit, the 2008-09 trade collapse, the Chilean salmon disease crisis) and import competition. He also analyses aquaculture regulation, quota rents, sea lice control with cleaner fish, and price volatility in oil and storage markets.

name: Ayda Joudavi
summary: Ayda Joudavi studies how digital tools and incentives can encourage sustainable behaviour in cities and companies. Her work combines literature review, policy document analysis, stakeholder engagement and mixed-method index development, with case studies in Stavanger, Norwegian businesses and Gdańsk. Application areas include commuter cycling, circular economy adoption across sectors, and reward schemes for residents' pro-environmental actions.

name: Bjørn Ivar Kruke
summary: Bjørn Ivar Kruke studies crisis management, risk governance and emergency preparedness, using mainly qualitative methods such as interviews, case studies and literature reviews alongside conceptual and typology development. His work covers police decision-making in armed confrontations, natural hazard evacuation and avalanche risk, flood and climate adaptation, and trust and communication in Arctic communities such as Longyearbyen. He also examines resilience, social capital and improvisation in the 2011 Norwegian terror attack, school preparedness for life-threatening violence, and governance of Arctic cruise ship noise.

name: Brynhild Stavland
summary: Brynhild Stavland studies how safety regulation can be designed for hydrogen as an energy carrier as it is adopted more widely in society. Her work applies a systems-theory approach based on Leveson's methods to analyse the regulatory system, identifying hazards and constraints relevant to regulating hydrogen. The work is relevant to energy transition policy, regulators and industry planning for large-scale hydrogen use.

name: Chinwe Philomina Oramah
summary: Chinwe Philomina Oramah studies how climate change is framed as a security issue in Nigeria and what that framing means for adaptation policy and practice. Using securitization theory with primary and secondary data, the work examines climate policies and action plans alongside people's vulnerability and adaptation. The research sits in climate governance and policy analysis, with attention to the socio-political factors that shape adaptation outcomes.

name: Christian Henrik Alexander Kuran
summary: Christian Henrik Alexander Kuran studies safety and risk in heavy goods road transport, crisis and disaster management, and professional education for customs and border work. His work uses document analysis, scoping and meta-ethnographic reviews, accident investigation reports, diaries, interviews and thematic analysis. It covers how rule bending arises from regulation and market pressure, the roles of social capital and resilience in crises, and how students and organisations learn from practice.

name: Claudia Morsut
summary: Claudia Morsut studies how climate change adaptation is governed, focusing on risk management and the securitisation or riskification of climate policy at international, national and local levels. Her work uses document and discourse analysis, interviews and comparative case studies of the UN, the EU, Norway, Sweden, the Netherlands and European cities, drawing on Security Studies and Risk Governance. She also works on disaster risk management, including methods for defining and identifying good practices, flood risk and preparedness, and vulnerability and policy metrics in the COVID-19 pandemic.

name: Cristian Tosa
summary: Cristian Tosa studies sustainability transitions, focusing on household energy behaviour, smart energy apps, circular economy, and urban and rural development. His work uses text mining, sentiment analysis and topic modelling of app reviews and Twitter/X data, together with surveys, stated-preference experiments, systematic reviews and stakeholder-based frameworks. Application areas include Norwegian households and companies, Romanian and Eastern European housing and building stocks, Polish city incentives, smart city narratives and nature-based stormwater solutions.

name: Daniela Müller-Eie
summary: Daniela Müller-Eie studies sustainable urban mobility and planning, with a focus on combining bicycles and public transport, travel behaviour, and transport equity in Norwegian regions such as Nord-Jæren. Her methods include survey-based structural equation modelling, spatial accessibility and equity analysis, systematic literature review and policy document analysis. She also examines smart sustainable city development in Stavanger and other Nordic cities, and the links between housing, neighbourhood conditions and quality of life for local and immigrant residents.

name: David Chapman
summary: David Chapman works on urban design and planning for settlements in the Arctic, with a focus on small, remote cities in the European Arctic and comparisons with North America, Russia, Iceland, Greenland and China. His publications examine place-shaping, microclimate, cultural heritage, and movement and transport as factors in making northern cities attractive places to live. The work is aimed at students and practitioners of architecture, urban design and town planning.

name: Dikshya Bhandari
summary: Dikshya Bhandari studies safety, reliability and risk assessment of hydrogen energy systems. Her work includes a qualitative comparison of risk analysis frameworks and guidelines used by Norwegian regulators across maritime, civil protection and offshore sectors, and an examination of dynamic and multistate fault tree methods applied to hydrogen storage explosion scenarios. Both studies address how uncertainty and strength of knowledge are treated, with the aim of supporting more consistent safety practice and decision-making in hydrogen applications.

name: Eirik Bjorheim Abrahamsen
summary: Eirik Bjorheim Abrahamsen studies risk assessment and safety in high-hazard operations, using multi-criteria decision analysis, evidence reasoning, time series forecasting, systems thinking and hazard analysis. Application areas include explosive remnants of war, helicopter rescue (workload and procedures), and offshore decommissioning regulation. He also researches higher education, covering learning from practice in customs and border management, supervisor training, teaching quality during COVID-19, class size, exam appeals and learning management system adoption, mostly through student data, surveys, diaries and thematic analysis.

name: Eivind Lorentzen-Styr
summary: Eivind Lorentzen-Styr studies how knowledge and uncertainty are handled in risk assessment, focusing on the strength of knowledge concept and a proposed extension, strength of justification, that also considers how knowledge is turned into probability and risk judgments. The work combines conceptual and methodological analysis with an interview study of 22 risk practitioners in Norway who use strength of knowledge schemes. Application areas include public and private sector risk assessment standards, guidance and risk communication.

name: Fabio Alberto Hernandez Palacio
summary: Fabio Alberto Hernandez Palacio studies how urban form, especially density and compactness, relates to accessibility, sustainability and quality of life in cities. His work combines GIS network analysis, walking and cycling isochrones, statistical comparison, field observation and practitioner surveys, applied to case studies in Norwegian cities such as Stavanger and Tromsø. Application areas include 10-minute and proximity-based planning, access to services and open spaces, and energy efficiency and solar access in Arctic urban design.

name: Farnaz Eskandari
summary: Farnaz Eskandari studies how climate and environmental stressors affect urban traffic safety, using machine learning on remote sensing data. Her Austin, Texas work compares several algorithms, explains the results with SHAP analysis, and builds a combined vulnerability index to map where crash risk is highest. The research serves urban planning and transport safety applications.

name: Frank Asche
summary: Frank Asche studies the economics of fisheries and aquaculture, with emphasis on salmon, shrimp, cod and catfish, and on global seafood production, trade and supply chains. His work uses econometric methods such as cointegration analysis, firm-level and customs trade data, instrumental variables, stochastic bioeconomic simulation, web search data and literature reviews. Topics include import competition and pricing, ecolabel premiums, industry clustering, disease and parasite management, production risk in recirculating systems, and the sustainability and governance of seafood sectors in Norway, Indonesia, the EU and the US.

name: Frederic Emmanuel Bouder
summary: Frederic Emmanuel Bouder studies how risks and scientific uncertainty are perceived, communicated and governed by public authorities. Using survey-based structural equation modelling, ethnographic fieldwork, case studies, policy analysis and systematic literature review, the work covers COVID-19 mitigation behaviour, food safety regulation, the Dutch energy transition, crisis management and artificial intelligence. A recurring focus is how trust, public perceptions and tolerability-of-risk concepts can inform decisions by regulators and policymakers.

name: Geir Petter Novik
summary: Geir Petter Novik studies the safety and risk management of explosive remnants of war, including unexploded ordnance, dumped munitions and munition-laden shipwrecks. His work combines laboratory analysis of aged explosives (impact and thermal sensitivity testing, spectroscopy and chromatography) with statistical methods such as maximum likelihood estimation, and with qualitative case studies and systems-based approaches to risk assessment under uncertainty. Applications include military and defence organisations, environmental protection, societal safety and the handling of hazardous chemicals such as peroxide-forming solvents.

name: Guicang Peng
summary: Guicang Peng studies operational risk assessment and management, developing mathematical models that balance multiple objectives and handle uncertain, conflicting or fast-changing information. The methods include evidence reasoning, multi-criteria decision analysis (TOPSIS) and time series forecasting (SARIMA), alongside literature reviews, industry surveys and case study analysis. Application areas include well control and process safety in onshore drilling in Iraq and country-level risk mapping using real-time conflict event data.

name: Harald Nils Røstvik
summary: Harald Nils Røstvik studies building energy performance, focusing on how calculated values in energy performance certificates compare with measured energy use in non-residential buildings. His work examines ten recently built municipal buildings in Sandnes, Norway, comparing calculated and measured energy at whole-building, energy-carrier and end-use levels, and introduces an index showing how opposing errors cancel in aggregate totals. The findings apply to certificate validation, sub-metering and building performance evaluation.

name: Håkon Bjorheim Abrahamsen
summary: Håkon Bjorheim Abrahamsen studies safety and risk in helicopter emergency medical service rescue work as well as teaching quality and student satisfaction in higher education. His work uses hazard identification through Safe Job Analysis, retrospective analysis of mission records, and large-scale analysis of student survey and course evaluation data from the University of Stavanger. Application areas include static rope and offset rescue procedures in Norway and the management of university teaching during the COVID-19 pandemic.

name: Ingrid Glette-Iversen
summary: Ingrid Glette-Iversen works in risk science, focusing on how risk, uncertainty and knowledge are defined, characterized and communicated. Her publications use conceptual analysis and literature review to examine ideas such as plausibility, unpredictable events and "real risk", and to propose improvements to risk management and decision-making frameworks. She applies this work to hydrogen safety regulation in Norway, COVID-19 risk assessment, vaccine risk and climate change research.

name: Ioannis Kosmidis
summary: Ioannis Kosmidis studies sustainable urban transport, with a focus on combining bicycles and public transport, transport equity and accessibility, and how attitudes shape travel behaviour, including electric car use. His work draws on survey data analysed with structural equation modelling, latent class analysis and ordinal regression, as well as spatial accessibility and equity indicators, scenario comparison, literature review and policy document analysis. Application areas include mid-sized Norwegian regions such as Nord-Jæren, Athens and Nordic smart cities, covering commuting, job accessibility, road space allocation and urban mobility planning.

name: Jacob Taarup-Esbensen
summary: Jacob Taarup-Esbensen studies risk analysis, business continuity and resilience in Arctic settings, using conceptual models, case studies, bow-tie analysis, interviews, archival material and on-site observations. His work covers how organizations make sense of uncertainty, how a mining company on Svalbard managed a flooding event, hazards to shipping supply chains around Baffin Bay and Greenland, and how remote Greenlandic communities could withstand a tsunami. The applications are in safety and emergency preparedness for mining, maritime transport and community disaster management.

name: Jason Deegan
summary: Jason Deegan studies regional innovation policy and economic diversification, with a focus on Smart Specialisation strategies and the entrepreneurial discovery process in European and Norwegian regions. His work combines quantitative analysis of linked employer-employee data and regional industry structure with qualitative methods such as document analysis and stakeholder interviews. It addresses how regions choose priority domains, how policy ideas are interpreted locally, and how regions move into new jobs through related industries and occupations.

name: Jon Tømmerås Selvik
summary: Jon Tømmerås Selvik works on risk, reliability and safety management, with a strong focus on hydrogen systems and on petroleum activities such as well abandonment, decommissioning, oil spill preparedness and safety-critical equipment testing. His methods include fault tree analysis, FMEA, multi-criteria decision analysis, evidence reasoning, time series forecasting and imperfect repair modelling, along with qualitative comparisons of regulations and standards. He also writes on decision quality and systems thinking in higher education, including exam appeal schemes.

name: Kenneth Arne Pettersen Gould
summary: Kenneth Arne Pettersen Gould studies how risk is perceived, communicated and managed in organisations and society, including the social amplification and attenuation of risk, public trust in government during crises, and the role of experts. His work also covers safety and reliability in inter-organisational settings such as construction projects, publicly procured air ambulance services and smart city critical infrastructure. Methods are mainly qualitative case studies, fieldwork, interviews and literature reviews, supplemented by analysis of repeated survey data and policy documents.

name: Kjartan Bjørnsen
summary: Kjartan Bjørnsen studies how uncertainty is characterised and handled in risk assessment, drawing on risk science concepts. His work includes interviews with 22 Norwegian risk practitioners on how they use strength of knowledge schemes, and a conceptual analysis of Norwegian environmental impact assessment regulation and guidelines as a form of risk assessment. The research is aimed at improving the guidance, terminology and practical use of risk assessment in public and private sectors.

name: Kjell Hausken
summary: Kjell Hausken studies strategic conflict and decision-making using game theory, differential and stochastic models, and simulation. His work covers counterterrorism, economic sanctions, military force modeling in the Lanchester tradition, infrastructure security and reliability, and the competition among cryptocurrencies, fiat and hard money. He also carries out bibliometric reviews of fields such as Bitcoin and green finance, and reviews game theory applied to pandemics, disasters and social media rumors.

name: Knut Erik Bang
summary: Knut Erik Bang studies operational risk management, covering well control in onshore drilling, country-level risk mapping, and adaptive risk assessment. The work combines case study analysis, literature reviews, industry surveys, and quantitative modelling that pairs time series forecasting with multicriteria decision analysis, using real-time conflict event data in Python. Application areas include oil and gas drilling, process safety, and international operations exposed to geopolitical and other external threats.

name: Kristin Helen Roll
summary: Kristin Helen Roll studies the economics of fisheries and aquaculture, covering fisheries management, vessel capacity and efficiency, fuel taxation, salmon trade and price risk, and industry clustering. Her methods include difference-in-differences, data envelopment analysis, Tobit regression, firm-level trade analysis and price correlation tests, applied mainly to Norwegian and Nordic fisheries, Norwegian salmon farming and Bangladeshi artisanal fisheries. She has also co-authored a recent mixed-methods evaluation of interactive welfare technology for nursing home residents with dementia.

name: Lasse Berg Andersen
summary: Lasse Berg Andersen works on environmental risk assessment for marine aquaculture, with a focus on methods grounded in risk science. His work develops and applies an assessment approach, tested in a study of Norwegian fish farming, that supports shared understanding of risk among stakeholders with differing values. The application areas are environmental risk management, risk communication and risk-informed decision-making in sustainable aquaculture.

name: Lisa Jean Watson
summary: Lisa Jean Watson works on 3D documentation and geospatial analysis, using terrestrial laser scanning and point-cloud processing to record and measure archaeological sites such as Mycenaean chamber tombs in Greece, including semi-automatic detection of tool marks. Her work also combines ground-penetrating radar, drilling, aerial laser scanning and geological mapping to build 3D subsurface models of an urban area in Norway. She has also applied spatial multi-criteria evaluation and least-cost path analysis to road bypass planning in Botswana.

name: Lisbet Fjæran
summary: Lisbet Fjæran studies how risks are perceived, communicated and governed, with a focus on the social amplification and attenuation of risk, the part played by experts and other social actors, and public trust in government during risk events and crises. Her work uses conceptual and systems/network theory, case analysis, long-run survey trend data, and a scoping review protocol on emotionally framed health messages for adolescents. Application areas include food and feed safety, health communication, crisis management, and the regulation of petroleum industry safety.

name: Maria Korkou
summary: Maria Korkou studies urban green infrastructure and green spaces, focusing on how multiple functions and ecosystem services can be assessed and used in spatial planning. Her work combines indicator-based spatial assessment, correlation and multivariate analysis, systematic literature review, mapping, surveys, interviews and observations. Application areas include city-level green space planning in Stavanger, Norway, and the use of green spaces for outdoor learning and sustainability education among preschool and school children.

name: Marja Katariina Ylönen
summary: Marja Katariina Ylönen studies risk, safety and security from organisational and sociotechnical perspectives, building conceptual frameworks and applying qualitative methods such as thematic analysis, content analysis, interviews and crime script analysis. Her work covers integrated safety and security management in nuclear and Seveso industrial sites, regulation of risk in the Norwegian petroleum sector, and the foundations and internal tensions of risk science. She also examines customs and border control, including intelligence and risk management, smugglers' protective measures, cross-sector cooperation in societal security in Svalbard, and learning from practice in customs education.

name: Morten Sommer
summary: Morten Sommer studies safety and risk management under high uncertainty, with a focus on explosive remnants of war and unexploded ordnance. He also studies organisational learning in emergency and police organisations, covering exercises, evaluation and follow-up. His work relies mainly on qualitative case studies, interviews and document analysis in Norwegian defence and emergency response settings, together with conceptual critiques of risk assessment methods and systems thinking.

name: Najmeh Mozaffaree Pour
summary: Najmeh Mozaffaree Pour works on urban sustainability and land governance, with a focus on post-growth planning at the neighborhood scale. Her publication develops a conceptual framework, built from a systematic scoping review, that assesses whether neighborhoods meet residents' needs within ecological limits and distribute services, green space and affordable space fairly. The framework links indicators and thresholds to governance instruments, and it is presented as a provisional tool for planners that still needs empirical testing.

name: Nita Santika
summary: Nita Santika studies international trade in seafood, using firm-level and highly disaggregated export data from Norway. Her work examines how exporters and importers respond to supply disruptions and uncertainty, including the Chilean salmon disease crisis and the Brexit referendum, and how regional clustering of exporters shapes export volumes, prices and new trade relationships. The studies apply empirical economic methods, including quasi-natural experiment designs, to questions about supply chain resilience in aquaculture and wild-harvest seafood.

name: Ole Andreas Hegland Engen
summary: Ole Andreas Hegland Engen studies risk governance and regulation, focusing on the Norwegian petroleum sector and on climate change adaptation. His work uses conceptual analysis, interviews, document analysis and comparative case studies of national and local governments (Norway, Sweden, the Netherlands and other European cities) to examine how safety, security and risk logics shape policy, oversight and tripartite cooperation. Application areas include offshore safety and security regulation, standardization, AI in safety management, flood risk and municipal climate adaptation.

name: Olena Mykolajivna Koval
summary: Olena Mykolajivna Koval studies how people and organisations make and communicate decisions under risk, using behavioural experiments, scoping reviews and content analysis. Her work covers how couples, individuals and random groups solve ill-structured problems in tourism, including under time pressure. It also covers how health authorities communicate pandemic risks to immigrants and to the public through social media in several European countries.

name: Ove Njå
summary: Ove Njå studies safety and risk in road tunnels and related transport and emergency response systems, covering tunnel fire evacuation, self-rescue, and the design of risk communication for road users. His work draws on virtual reality experiments, interviews, surveys with structural equation modelling, Poisson regression of fire incident data, document analysis and workshops. Application areas include fire and rescue service learning, heavy goods transport safety and rule bending, hospital surge capacity, fire safety engineering regulation, and public and stakeholder views on hydrogen safety.

name: Paulo Thiago Bastos Rocha
summary: Paulo Thiago Bastos Rocha studies intercultural communication and organizational culture in public-sector and educational settings. His work uses qualitative case study methods (document analysis, interviews, observation), survey-based correlation and regression analysis, and Cultural-Historical Activity Theory. Application areas include collaboration between criminal justice and welfare services in offender rehabilitation, intercultural competence and bias in customs officer education in Norway, and blended learning for international students in higher education.

name: Petter Osmundsen
summary: Petter Osmundsen studies the economics of energy projects, covering offshore wind and petroleum. His work applies econometric methods, including multivariate regression, quantile regression and learning-curve analysis, together with case-based project modelling, to UK offshore wind costs and output over time, oil and gas stock return risks, and how tax design shapes development concept choice and capital allocation. The work serves industry and government audiences interested in project profitability, subsidy and fiscal policy, and resource management.

name: Riana Steen
summary: Riana Steen studies probabilistic risk assessment and its use in decision support when uncertainty about likelihoods and consequences is large. Her work applies Bayesian Network modelling to risk-based inspection, using explosion-protected equipment in the Norwegian petroleum industry as a case. The approach combines varied data sources to build a dynamic cause-and-consequence risk picture, while examining data gaps and analyst subjectivity.

name: Roger Flage
summary: Roger Flage works on the foundations of risk science, focusing on how risk, uncertainty, probability and knowledge are conceptualized, characterized and communicated. His publications are mostly conceptual and methodological, covering frameworks for judging the strength of knowledge and justification, assumptions, unpredictable events and dynamic risk management, and the role of AI and data-driven models in risk analysis. Applied studies cover power outage hotspot analysis, environmental risk of deep-sea mining and offshore polymer discharges, vaccine risk, and security risks of digital twins.

name: Ruth Beatriz Pincinato
summary: Ruth Beatriz Pincinato studies the economics and management of fisheries and aquaculture, using econometric methods such as difference-in-differences, instrumental variables, demand and cointegration analysis, and structural modelling. Her work covers rights-based fisheries management, sea lice control and regulation in salmon farming, seafood trade and markets, and global comparisons of sustainability, gender participation and food security in seafood systems. She has also applied GIS and multi-criteria analysis to river restoration and floodplain reconnection for urban flood resilience in Brazil.

name: Ruth Østgaard Skotnes
summary: Ruth Østgaard Skotnes studies how public bodies and industry organize and communicate risk, with a focus on Nordic municipalities, critical infrastructure and emerging energy technologies. Her work uses qualitative methods such as focus groups and semi-structured interviews, along with organizational and systems perspectives, to examine ownership of risk communication, integration of safety and security management in smart cities, and stakeholder perception of hydrogen in Norway.

name: Sasan Zarghooni-Hoffmann
summary: Sasan Zarghooni-Hoffmann studies societal security, organised crime and intelligence analysis, drawing on systems theory, risk science and qualitative methods. The publications develop a boundary-based framework for cross-sector cooperation tested in Svalbard case studies, apply thematic crime script analysis to Norwegian court verdicts on smuggling, and adapt risk science's strength-of-knowledge concepts to judge the quality of intelligence assessments. Application areas include customs and border control, law enforcement detection and investigation, and critical infrastructure protection.

name: Sigbjørn Landazuri Tveteraas
summary: Sigbjørn Landazuri Tveteraas studies the economics of tourism, hospitality and seafood industries, mainly in Norway. Using econometric methods such as cointegration and threshold autoregressive models to examine price links between Airbnb and hotels, and stochastic frontier analysis to measure hotel staffing and management efficiency, he also draws on surveys, interviews and regional case studies. His work further covers the use of fish by-products for fishmeal and fish oil in several countries, and how tourism destinations adapt to crises such as COVID-19.

name: Sindre Lorentzen
summary: Sindre Lorentzen studies the economics and project performance of offshore wind, with a focus on UK wind farms. Using econometric analysis of capital cost and capacity factor data, project profitability modelling and descriptive statistics of project activity data, the work examines cost drivers, learning effects, production over a wind farm's life cycle, oil company investment returns and construction productivity including pandemic disruption. The findings relate to energy industry investors, policymakers and project managers.

name: Sissel Haugdal Jore
summary: Sissel Haugdal Jore studies how safety and security are governed and understood, with a focus on terrorism, hybrid threats and societal resilience. Her work uses qualitative interviews, document analysis, and conceptual and discourse analysis, applied to the Norwegian petroleum sector, security guards, public procurement of security services and urban counterterrorism. It also examines regulatory models, ethical tensions and the role of private companies as security actors.

name: Tegg Westbrook
summary: Tegg Westbrook studies the security of satellite navigation and positioning systems, focusing on radiofrequency jamming and spoofing and the motives behind them. The publications use literature-based analysis and taxonomy building to examine threats to autonomous vehicles, maritime traffic and geopolitical rivalries, as well as emergency response in smart 15-minute cities. The work addresses implications for city planning, urban security, vehicle safety and international relations.

name: Terje Aven
summary: Terje Aven works on the foundations of risk science, focusing on how risk is conceptualized, described and judged in terms of uncertainty, knowledge strength, probability and potential surprises. His publications use conceptual analysis, framework development, practitioner interviews, text analysis and case illustrations (such as the Boeing 737 Max, 9/11 and the Bovaer controversy) to examine risk study quality, ethics and systemic factors. Application areas include safety science, public guidance such as United Nations risk assessment documents, economics and decision analysis, and risk governance and regulation.

name: Todor Milkov Kesarovski
summary: Todor Milkov Kesarovski studies how urban density relates to air quality and to residents' access to services and open spaces, mainly in Norwegian cities such as Stavanger, Oslo, Bergen and Trondheim. His work combines GIS network and isochrone analysis, open data, regression models and field observation, and also includes survey and interview work on kindergarten teachers' awareness of air quality. The findings are aimed at urban planning, transport and sustainability policy, including electric vehicle uptake and the 10-minute city concept.

name: Tonja Knapstad
summary: Tonja Knapstad studies how structured risk communication shapes the way road users behave and learn when a fire occurs in a road tunnel. Her work combines a randomised controlled trial in a virtual reality driving simulator with follow-up qualitative interviews one and two years later, using a mixed-methods design. The research addresses road tunnel safety, public information campaigns and the role of users' competence in system safety and risk assessment.

name: Tore Markeset
summary: Tore Markeset works on operational risk, safety and asset management for oil and gas operations and power distribution infrastructure. His publications develop risk assessment models and frameworks using evidence reasoning, multi-criteria decision analysis (TOPSIS, AHP), fuzzy inference, fault tree and failure mode analysis, and time series forecasting. They are applied to well control in onshore drilling, overhead power cables, country risk mapping, and digitalized lifecycle management and life cycle costing of equipment.

name: Anders Vassenden
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Anders Vassenden is a sociologist who uses Goffman-inspired interactionist theory to study stigma, face-saving and emotional rituals in everyday encounters, drawing on ethnography and qualitative interviews. His empirical work covers ethnic minority experiences in Norway, such as responses to ethnoracial stigma and Norwegian Somali parents' fears of child protective services, as well as how elites and professors downplay their status. He also studies class, taste and morality using photo elicitation, street-level bureaucracy and migrant labour market integration in the welfare administration, platform work among taxi drivers, and the methodological use of situationalism in interviews.

name: Ann Karin Tennås Holmen
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Ann Karin Tennås Holmen studies governance and institutional change in digital transformation, covering both public-sector digitalisation and critical digital infrastructure. Her work uses qualitative case studies and conceptual modelling, drawing on metagovernance, institutional logics and collaborative platform theory. Application areas include Norwegian digital backbone infrastructure such as subsea cables, data centres and content delivery networks, regional digital government institutions, and the way innovative ideas interact with existing institutions.

name: Benjamin Ronald Silvester
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Benjamin Ronald Silvester studies sustainability transitions in energy systems, with a focus on the politics of cross-border electricity interconnection, North Sea grid integration and European decarbonisation and energy security. His work combines qualitative case analysis of Norway and Europe with theoretical frameworks, including a techno-economic-political feasibility framework and a relational theory of the state. He also critically examines carbon capture, utilisation and storage technologies, including an industrial case study of a Norwegian ferrosilicon plant.

name: Bjørn-Tore Blindheim
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences

name: Busra Yalcinoz-Ucan
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Busra Yalcinoz-Ucan studies gender-based violence and intimate partner violence, with a focus on technology-facilitated abuse, digital coercive control and digital inequalities, as well as help-seeking barriers among queer people in Norway. The work relies mainly on qualitative interviews with survivors and service practitioners, reflexive thematic analysis, and participatory visual methods such as digital storytelling and photovoice, within a feminist framework. It also examines how survivors in Turkey disclose violence online and seek informal justice, and draws implications for service provision, technology design and policy.

name: Carlo Michael Knotz
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Carlo Michael Knotz studies public attitudes towards the welfare state, including perceptions of who deserves benefits and services such as childcare, student finance and pandemic aid, and how these relate to immigration, ideology and psychological traits like social dominance orientation. He mainly uses original survey, vignette and conjoint experiments across multiple Western countries, and also carries out comparative analysis of welfare conditionality in OECD and Latin American countries. A further strand examines how technological change and AI-related job risks shape policy preferences and party support, especially among the higher-educated, along with refugee labour market integration.

name: Cato Wittusen
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Cato Wittusen studies how professionals and expert organizations exercise agency when complying with institutional rules, working within organizational institutionalism and practice theory. His conceptual, philosophical approach draws on Wittgenstein's ideas about rule-following and on Kantian thought to distinguish routine compliance from more reflective compliance in difficult cases. The work applies to professional expertise in rule-governed organizations and regulatory settings.

name: Cecilie Larsen
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Cecilie Larsen studies how news media frame conflicts over renewable energy development, with a focus on wind power on Fovsen in Norwegian Saepmie. Using discourse theory and analysis of local, regional, national and Saami news coverage from 2006 to 2023, her work traces how competing narratives justify or contest wind turbines and affect Saami reindeer herding. The research connects to social science debates on the green transition, Indigenous rights and energy policy.

name: Dian Liu
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Dian Liu studies higher education and schooling, with a focus on gender and career advancement among academics, workplace wellbeing and bullying among university staff, and burnout among teachers in China. The work also covers higher education policy such as international student tuition fees in Norway, sustainability and graduate entrepreneurship in China's Greater Bay Area, and digital parenting and the concept of habitus in education. Methods include interviews, case studies, surveys with moderation and mediation analysis, and umbrella and meta-ethnographic reviews.

name: Elin Merethe Oftedal
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Elin Merethe Oftedal studies how older adults adopt digital health technology and take part in innovation, using consumer studies and qualitative methods such as interviews, questionnaires and focus groups. She also researches sustainable value creation and business models, including a case study of a carbon capture and utilization project with microalgae, and a longitudinal study of startup companies. Her work spans healthcare, user inclusion, entrepreneurship and sustainable manufacturing.

name: Elisabeth Lund Engebretsen
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Elisabeth Lund Engebretsen studies feminist, queer and Indigenous activism and the politics of gender, race and belonging, with a focus on China and the Nordic region. Her work uses case studies, content and discourse analysis of social media, and edited collaborative volumes to examine anti-gender campaigns, climate justice and Sámi rights, and online attacks on academics. The research relates to gender equality policy, social movements, digital platforms and academic freedom.

name: Ellen Jenny Torgersen Ravndal
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Ellen Jenny Torgersen Ravndal studies the early history of the United Nations, focusing on the first Secretary-General, Trygve Lie, and how the organization moved from founding documents to working practice. Her book examines crisis decision-making, institutional constraints and the roles of individuals in shaping the secretary-general's office, and speaks to wider questions of how intergovernmental organizations are created, governed and gain autonomy. The work is historical and institutional in approach, and the publications listed include an entry on archives.

name: Ezgi Pehlivanli
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Ezgi Pehlivanli studies how politics, gender and digital media shape academic life, public discourse and everyday practices in Turkey. Using qualitative methods such as in-depth interviews, content analysis of social media posts and websites, and critical literature review, her work covers academic freedom and well-being among gender studies scholars, online academic harassment, populism and ideology in political projects like Canal Istanbul, and reproductive autonomy and anti-vaccine discourse.

name: Feodosiya Pavlovna Ermakova
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences

name: Geir Sverre Braut
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Geir Sverre Braut works on risk regulation and safety oversight, with one publication on offshore oil and gas and another on maternity care in Norway. His offshore study reviews regulatory strategies, institutions and legal traditions in Norway and the US, and combines them with empirical data to build a model for identifying effective regulation based on industry intentions, resources, expertise and mutual trust between industry and regulator. The listed work applies regulatory and policy analysis to high-risk industry and to health services.

name: Gunnar Thesen
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Gunnar Thesen studies political communication and party competition, focusing on how news media cover parties and politicians and how that coverage relates to electoral outcomes. His work uses large-scale computational text analysis of news corpora, combined with parliamentary speech, polling and election data, in comparative and longitudinal designs across European countries. Topics include newspaper alignment with parties, the tone of coverage of governing parties, the news visibility of legislators, and gender differences in media attention.

name: Hande Eslen Ziya
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Hande Eslen Ziya studies gender, populism and knowledge politics, with a focus on anti-gender movements, the manosphere and incel communities, and the online harassment of academics. Her work uses interviews, a prototype-based qualitative method, visual and discourse analysis of social media, and statistical modelling of legislator data, with cases mainly from Turkey as well as Hungary, Sweden and Norway. Application areas include academic freedom and well-being, women's political careers, protest aesthetics, and migrant access to teaching professions.

name: Helle Sjøvaag
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Helle Sjøvaag studies the political economy of news and communication industries, focusing on media ownership, market concentration, and journalism's growing dependence on platforms, AI and internet backbone infrastructure such as cables, data centres and content delivery networks. Her work uses methods including market revenue comparisons, large-scale computational analysis of newspapers and social media engagement, tracker analysis of government websites, interviews, discourse analysis and co-creation workshops. The main application areas are Nordic and Scandinavian media systems, local and public service journalism, digital governance and regulation, and datafication in smart cities and e-government.

name: Ingvil Førland Hellstrand
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Ingvil Førland Hellstrand studies gender, technology and culture from a feminist theory perspective, using critical analysis of science fiction films and cyberpunk alongside real-life conversational AI such as Siri, Alexa and Replika. She also carries out a scoping review of how care ethics is applied in empirical studies of technology-mediated healthcare. In addition, she writes on feminist transformative pedagogy in gender studies teaching, drawing on Donna Haraway's ideas.

name: Iryna Fyshchuk
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Iryna Fyshchuk studies digital transformation and cybersecurity in public administration, focusing on local authorities in Ukraine. Her work draws on qualitative, semi-structured interviews with public officials and on policy analysis to examine how communities manage cyberattacks during wartime and what limits or supports digitalization. She also looks at Ukraine-EU cooperation programs and at resource, staffing and skills constraints in public-sector digital governance.

name: Janina Jasper
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Janina Jasper studies how the governance and institutional design of electricity markets shapes demand-side flexibility in energy transitions. Her work uses institutional theory and qualitative analysis of policy and regulatory frameworks in a multi-sited comparison of the Netherlands and Japan. It looks at who can participate in flexibility schemes and how costs and benefits are distributed, with relevance for energy policy and market design.

name: Jens Kaae Fisker
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Jens Kaae Fisker studies urban and rural governance, participatory planning and sustainability transitions, drawing on case studies, participatory methods such as photography, sketching and futures workshops, and online ethnography. His work examines how inhabitants, including marginalised groups, take part in shaping places, from neighbourhood development and smart city planning in Stavanger to self-governing networks and online community groups in rural Denmark. He also develops theoretical frameworks, based on state theory and metagovernance, for understanding the role of the state and power in societal transformations toward sustainability.

name: Kristian Skagen Ekeli
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Kristian Skagen Ekeli works in constitutional theory and political philosophy, with a focus on how constitutional democracies can protect the interests of present and future generations through environmental rights. His normative analysis compares procedural rights that govern legislative processes with substantive rights such as a right to a healthy environment. He examines how vagueness in substantive rights affects judicial enforcement, democratic values and the rule of law.

name: Kristiane Marie Fjær Lindland
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Kristiane Marie Fjær Lindland studies how people take part in shaping futures and designing new solutions, in urban development and in product development. Her work uses case studies, including a neighbourhood in Stavanger, Norway and a porcelain company, and draws on participatory methods such as photography and utopian sketching alongside democratic theory and pragmatist perspectives on identity. Application areas include sustainable urban development, citizen-led futures work and collective creativity in design practice.

name: Lene Myong
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Lene Myong studies reproduction, kinship and racialization in the Nordic countries, with a focus on transnational adoption, child removal, surrogacy and marriage migration. Her work draws on critical analysis of legal, political and educational documents, alongside ethnographic material, and uses decolonial, biopolitical and gender studies perspectives. It addresses colonial legacies in Denmark, Norway and Greenland, state governance of families and belonging, and how climate change shapes reproductive decisions.

name: Liv Sunnercrantz
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Liv Sunnercrantz studies populist politics and political discourse, using discourse theory, rhetorical analysis and feminist perspectives. Her work examines how right-wing populist actors in Turkey, Hungary and Sweden use anti-gender narratives, and how experts and expertise are positioned in populist projects, including during COVID-19. She also analyses public debate on fossil-fuel investment and climate risk in Norway, looking at how challengers to the dominant view redescribe the issue.

name: Martin Søyland
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Martin Søyland studies legislative politics, with a focus on how party groups in the Norwegian parliament (the Storting) behave. His work, as shown by this 2025 publication, examines party group cohesion and the mechanisms of discipline that shape how members of parliament act collectively. The application domain is parliamentary decision-making and party organization in Norway.

name: Merete Hermansen Jonvik
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Merete Hermansen Jonvik is a sociologist who studies participation in arts and urban development, and how taste, class and morality shape cultural boundaries. Her work relies on qualitative methods, including in-depth ethnography, oral interviews and photo elicitation, with cases in Norway such as an informal urban development initiative and a study of taste in Stavanger. Application areas include citizen involvement in city development, and cultural judgement in the visual arts, literature and housing and architecture.

name: Oluf Langhelle
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Oluf Langhelle studies the social and political dimensions of energy and sustainability transitions, including public acceptance of carbon capture, utilisation and storage, and debates over whether captured CO2 should count as a resource. The publications also cover energy communities, justice and solidarity in energy social science, and the role of intermediaries and boundary spanners in urban experimentation. Work draws on case studies in Norway and Poland, qualitative social research and conceptual analysis, with attention to global renewable energy and geostrategic competition.

name: Ozan Félix Sousbois
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Ozan Félix Sousbois studies masculinities and online gender politics, focusing on incel and looksmaxxing communities within the manosphere, including how avatars, body modification, pain and influencer culture turn grievance into protest masculinity. The work uses netnography and visual and aesthetic analysis of online forums and platforms, and also reflects on the ethics and risks of queer researchers working in hostile fieldwork settings. Earlier work looks at masculinity, material objects and public Islam in Turkey.

name: Raul Ferrer Conill
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Raul Ferrer Conill studies how digital media, data and infrastructure shape journalism, public communication and governance, with a focus on Scandinavia. The work uses interviews, expert co-creation sessions, large-scale analysis of social media and website tracking data, legal and policy analysis, and systematic and scoping reviews. Application areas include news distribution and platform dependency, smart city data practices, government data tracking, AI policy in journalism, health messaging for adolescents, and audiovisual science communication.

name: Renée Margaritha Scharnigg
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Renée Margaritha Scharnigg studies the social, political and regulatory dimensions of solar PV and energy community development, with a focus on Portugal. Her work combines interviews and fieldwork, media and document analysis, and scenario-based quantitative comparison of energy-sharing models. It addresses energy justice, gender, accountability, intermediaries, geopolitics and policy design for renewable energy transitions.

name: Stanislav Stedronsky
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Stanislav Stedronsky studies how higher education can support sustainability, focusing on the competencies students need to act as change agents in line with the Sustainable Development Goals. His work links Education for Sustainable Development with theories of sustainability transitions and uses an exploratory case study of Norwegian universities to identify obstacles to competence-based teaching. It also examines a novel simulation game as a practice-oriented teaching tool.

name: Terje Hillesund
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Terje Hillesund studies how people read and write scholarly and digital texts, drawing on theories of embodied and distributed cognition and on affordance theory. His work uses observational interviews with academics to examine how reading, writing and digital publishing are linked through printouts, screens and online tools. He also develops conceptual frameworks that treat the body, the text's material form and technology as parts of one reading process.

name: Tevfik Murat Yildirim
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Tevfik Murat Yildirim is a political scientist who studies legislative behaviour, political communication, public opinion and gender in politics, with a strong focus on Turkey, the UK and the US. His work combines large-scale datasets, including parliamentary speeches, news coverage and decades of survey responses, with text coding, panel and regression models, causal designs such as difference-in-differences, and survey experiments. Application areas include voter turnout, women's political careers, media attention to politicians, emotive rhetoric, policy priorities, and partisan reactions to misinformation and elite cues.

name: Thomas Michael Sattich
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Thomas Michael Sattich studies the politics and geopolitics of energy transitions, including renewable energy policy, energy security perceptions, and the geopolitics of oceans and canals, with a regional focus on the Baltic Sea Region, Lithuania and Poland. His work uses case studies, policy analysis and social research on public acceptance of technologies such as carbon capture and storage. He also researches higher education for sustainability, developing and evaluating simulation games to teach climate negotiation and sustainability competencies.

name: Torvald Øgaard
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Torvald Øgaard studies how people experience and respond to service and work environments, using survey-based quantitative research and meta-analysis. His publications examine how perceived crowding and emotions shape satisfaction and loyalty among skiers at a ski resort, and how workplace incivility relates to employees' intentions to leave across sectors and countries. The work applies to tourism and visitor attraction management and to organizational and human resource settings.

name: Turid Borgen
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences

name: Ugo Corte
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Ugo Corte is a sociologist who develops theory on group culture, community and emotion, using qualitative and ethnographic evidence. His work examines how profanity builds belonging in workplaces such as war-zone trauma units, kitchens, wildfire crews and prisons, and how cruelty can become a source of shared pleasure in gangs, bullying and military settings. He also writes essays on sociological theorizing, anonymity, uncertainty and the legacy of Howard Becker's work on art worlds and collaborative circles.

name: Xia Sun
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Xia Sun studies gender and career advancement in higher education, focusing on how female researchers in Norway navigate institutional policies, gender roles, relationships and personal goals. The work uses empowerment as an analytical framework and draws on interview data to examine how structural and individual factors shape recognition and progression. It is relevant to institutional policy design aimed at supporting women's academic careers.

name: Yonas Tesema
department: Department of Media and Social Sciences
summary: Yonas Tesema studies the social and economic dimensions of industrial and energy change, using qualitative methods such as stakeholder interviews and ethnographic fieldwork. His recent work in Stavanger, Norway looks at community and stakeholder views of positive energy districts, firm-level decarbonization in feed manufacturing, and collaboration among stakeholders in sustainability transformation. His earlier work in Ethiopia's Bole Lemi Industrial Park examines labour governance in foreign garment factories, the aspirations of rural women migrant workers, and fieldwork access in factory settings.

name: Aksel Leknes
summary: Aksel Leknes works on automated analysis of infant brain MRI, focusing on volumetry from ultra-low-field scanners that are more accessible in low- and middle-income settings. His publication presents an open-source segmentation pipeline built on age-specific templates and priors, checked against high-field MRI references using correlation and percentage-error measures across infant cohorts in South Africa and Uganda. The pipeline is applied to regional brain growth, sex differences and the effects of low birthweight in early development.

name: Aleksander Hagen Erga
summary: Aleksander Hagen Erga studies substance use disorders, mainly in people using multiple substances, through long-term cohort studies in Norwegian treatment settings that follow patients for up to six to eight years. His work links recovery outcomes to personality traits, cognitive impairment, childhood maltreatment, drug-free friendships, life satisfaction and psychological distress, using methods such as latent growth curve models, dynamic structural equation models and regression. He also helps design clinical trials, including a placebo-controlled trial of dextroamphetamine for amphetamine dependence and an online video-based cognitive behavioural therapy trial for depression in Parkinson's disease, and has contributed to work on cognitive decline in Parkinson's disease.

name: Aleksandra Sevic
summary: Aleksandra Sevic studies how people respond to digital technology and artificial intelligence, and how technology use and lifestyle factors relate to wellbeing at work. Her work uses questionnaire surveys, regression and factor analysis, scale translation and validation, and systematic reviews with meta-analysis. Application areas include public acceptance of AI across different uses, digital stress and exhaustion among employees in higher education, workplace eHealth interventions, and the link between alcohol use and sickness absence.

name: Ayo Zahra
summary: Ayo Zahra develops and validates open-source image analysis tools for measuring brain volumes from ultra-low-field MRI in infants and toddlers. The work uses age-specific templates and priors for automated segmentation, compares results against high-field MRI with correlation and percentage-error measures, and applies mixed-effects models to examine age, sex and birthweight. The application focus is accessible infant neuroimaging in low- and middle-income settings, with cohorts in South Africa and Uganda.

name: Bianka Anna Karshikoff
summary: Bianka Anna Karshikoff studies how inflammation relates to pain, sickness behavior and mental health, combining blood biomarker panels (cytokines and other inflammatory proteins), self-report questionnaires, brain imaging and multivariate statistics in clinical samples of people with chronic pain. Her work also uses experimental endotoxin-induced inflammation and seasonal allergy in healthy volunteers to examine how immune activation affects pain sensitivity and body odor perception, and includes validation of a sickness behavior questionnaire. She also examines whether baseline inflammation influences response to behavioral treatment and writes methodological and review pieces on omics-based biomarker research in psychoneuroimmunology.

name: Danilo Garcia
summary: Danilo Garcia studies personality, well-being and mental health, often through Cloninger's biopsychosocial model, with a focus on students, medical trainees, adolescents and older adults. His work combines survey studies using structural equation modeling, network analysis and regression with psychometric adaptation of questionnaires across countries, and with AI and language-model methods for assessing and delivering mental health care. Application areas include education, health care training, public and school health, physical activity, sustainable food systems and media psychology.

name: Francesco Margoni
summary: Francesco Margoni studies the development of moral and social cognition, including how infants and children reason about fairness, authority, leadership, cooperation and trust. His work uses looking-time experiments with infants, child and adult behavioral tasks across several countries, and surveys and vignette studies of adults, such as mock jurors, intelligence professionals and people judging robots. Applications span child development, human-robot interaction, legal decision-making and research methodology.

name: Jone Ravndal Bjørnestad
summary: Jone Ravndal Bjørnestad studies mental health and substance use recovery alongside consumer behavior in banking. Work on psychosis risk, substance use disorders and contraceptive prescribing draws on systematic reviews and meta-analyses, qualitative interviews and focus groups, and longitudinal modelling such as latent class and dynamic structural equation models. Work on banking uses representative survey and longitudinal data with regression and moderated mediation analyses to examine how satisfaction and self-efficacy relate to bank-switching intention and behavior. Further work covers a gaming-based intervention for unemployed young adults and training for foster care counselors.

name: Lilla Magyari
summary: Lilla Magyari studies how brains process speech and vocal sounds, using EEG and event-related potentials in humans, dogs and pigs to compare neural responses across species and to test whether dogs understand object words. Her work also covers human speech in multi-talker settings, prediction and turn-taking in conversation, speech patterns in political speeches, and how reading on screen versus print affects text comprehension among vocational students.

name: Liv Sand
summary: Liv Sand studies eating disorders and their overlap with personality disorders and perfectionism, combining clinical case work with large population-based survey research. The publications include a single-case study of cognitive behavioural therapy for adolescent anorexia nervosa with perfectionism, a commentary on integrated treatment of eating and personality disorders, and a prospective cohort study using logistic regression to link perfectionism to later depression among Norwegian higher education students. The work applies to clinical psychotherapy and to mental health prevention for young adults.

name: Marita Kallesten Brønnick
summary: Marita Kallesten Brønnick studies how hormonal contraceptives, especially the intrauterine system, are prescribed to adolescents and how this relates to mental health outcomes such as depression. Her work uses focus group interviews with healthcare professionals at Norwegian health centers, analysed thematically, to identify who is recommended which products and why. The findings are intended to help future quantitative studies account for selective prescribing as a source of confounding.

name: Muriel Marisa Katharina Bruchhage
summary: Muriel Marisa Katharina Bruchhage studies early brain development in infants and children using structural and functional MRI, including ultra-low-field scanners for use in low- and middle-income settings. Her work combines image-analysis pipelines, normative and longitudinal statistical models, and machine learning to examine how brain growth relates to maternal education and weight, genetics, gut microbiome, nutrition and cognition. She also contributes review work on the cerebellum in ageing.

name: Nicolay Gausel
summary: Nicolay Gausel studies moral emotions, especially shame, and how people account for wrongdoing, including sexual violence, using conversation analysis of research interviews with young people who have committed sexual violations. The work also covers psychometric testing of a therapy outcome-monitoring scale through confirmatory factor analysis with Norwegian clients, and social-psychological research on how national identification and shame relate to opposing prejudice toward immigrants. Application areas include social work practice, psychotherapy measurement and intergroup relations.

name: Pravin Tembjerg
summary: Pravin Tembjerg studies how separating children and young people from their families affects them, and how family relationships can be rebuilt or reunification pursued. The work, which appears as chapters in an edited volume, compares separation contexts such as child protection removal, institutional care, parental incarceration, divorce, migration and parental death. It draws on attachment, crisis, recognition and other social theories and links separation to children's mental health, with relevance to child welfare and helping professionals.

name: Synne Wiberg
summary: Synne Wiberg studies how digitalization affects people working in Norway's offshore petroleum industry, focusing on psychosocial factors such as cognitive demands, trust and workload. Her work combines in-depth interviews with offshore personnel and a narrative review of government and industry reports to compare workers' experiences of digital tools like handheld devices with industry priorities. The research applies to high-risk work settings where efficiency, safety and employee well-being need to be balanced.

name: Tore Tjora
summary: Tore Tjora studies behavior, mental health and work-related outcomes in Norwegian populations using surveys, registry data, longitudinal designs and psychometric validation. His work covers consumer bank-switching and self-efficacy, adolescent emotion regulation and adversity, psychosis risk and substance use, and safety climate and work disability in the petroleum and welfare sectors. Methods include regression, structural equation and latent class or growth models, decision-tree machine learning, and qualitative focus groups.

name: Vendela Husberg-Bru
